en: When Lord Kṛṣṇa Keśava was born in
Tirukkōṭṭiyūr, surrounded by decorated mansions
Sesame oil and [tumeric] powder were sprinkled, combining [with each other]
mixing [on the ground] of Kṛṣṇa’s court-yard such that it became mud
They run, they fall, rising, they shout
they seek [him], saying, “where is he, Our Lord?”
The cow-herd hamlet became [filled with] singers
dancers, and the continuous beating of many drums
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person
participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person
participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person
participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person
participial noun, third person, imperfective aspect
participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person, plural
participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person, plural

en: When, having been wished for, the child who possesses good qualities was born
those who entered to see him, entered and left saying
“this one is not like [other] men with virtue, see!
He whose [asterism is] Tiruvōṇa rules the world”
gloss: participial noun, third person, imperfective aspect
participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person
participial noun, third person, imperfective aspect

en: They dance continuously, whirling about the rope-shelf in the courtyard
they happily sprinkle fragrant ghee, milk, and curds
everywhere swinging to and fro such that [their] thick, soft tresses became loose
the cowherds of the cowherd village have lost their minds!
Those who collected the pole, the stick of the rope-shelf
and the cruel axe that had been grasped
those who have a palm-leaf mat for a bed
those who have teeth like jasmine buds that have not blossomed
[and] the cowherders gathered and entered the [village] and bathed with ghee
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, third person

en: When unfolding [his] arms and legs, gently bathing [him]
in the water of a cauldron, and opening [his] small mouth
to smear [his] tongue with a little [piece] of fresh tumeric
she saw the seven worlds in the mouth of the child
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, feminine, singular, dative

en: The good woman who saw the worlds in [his] mouth
[that] woman rejoiced, saying, “he is no son of a cowherd
[he is] the great Lord, Māyaṉ, the child who has qualities
[and] a nature that is pleasing"
[On] the second day after ten days
[they] erected a triumphal arch [on] all the cardinal points
[and] having awakened the son who held up the mountain of the must-elephant
the cowherds were pleased
If [he] lays down, [he] kicks so that the cradle breaks
If [he] is carried and held, [he] smashes the side of [my] body
If [he] is subdued and embraced, [he] pounces on [my] belly
Ladies! Because of being without strength, I have become weak
There is no evil for those who master this song of praise
that was expounded [by] Viṣṇu Cittaṉ [with] the shining text
[about] the birth of the eternal Lord Nāraṇaṉ [in] Tirukkōṭṭiyūr
surrounded by abundant agricultural tracts of superior paddy

ta: பாதக் கமலங்கள் காணீரே பவளவா யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: You with coral-red mouths, see the lotus-feet that are seized
and sucked and tasted [by] the innocent babe
who was sent to Yaśodā, with a garland in her curly hair, [by] Devakī
who is like the nectar in the cool sea. Come and see!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, vocative, third person

ta: ளொத்திட் டிருந்தவா காணீரே யொண்ணுத லீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: You with bright-foreheads, see the way the feet
of the gem-hued [Lord] and all [his] ten toes beat harmoniously and settle
every part [of him] is as if a gift of pearls, gems, and diamonds
collected and set in good gold. Come and see!
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, plural, vocative

ta: கணைக்கா லிருந்தவா காணீரே காரிகை யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: Ladies, see the way [his] shins shine permanently
with silver anklets on the pair of feet of this child who
after embracing the milk-gushing breasts of the young cowherdess with bamboo-like arms
drank, so that he became full, and slept. Come and see!

ta: முழந்தா ளிருந்தவா காணீரே முகிழ்முலை யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: You with bud[-like] breasts, see the quality of the knees of he who
crept [away] in terror [after he] ate each and every pot of the ghee
of she who suffered and she who lost [the ghee] dragged [him] with anger
and raised the old rope of a big churning stick to strike [him]. Come and see!
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, feminine, singular
participial noun, perfective aspect, singular, feminine
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular

ta: குறங்கு களைவந்து காணீரே குவிமுலை யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: You with round breasts, come and see the thighs
of he who long ago split the chest of the wrathful Hiraṇya
[of] this child, who sleeps like the one who slept
after eating, sucking the breast of the shining demoness. Come and see!
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular
participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

ta: முத்த மிருந்தவா காணீரே முகிழ்நகை யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: You smiling [ladies], see the quality of the penis of Acyuta
who appeared on the 10th day of Hastam from the womb of Devakī
who was not separate from the mind of Vasudeva with frenzied elephants
Come and see!
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, plural, vocative

ta: மருங்கு மிருந்தவா காணீரே வாணுத லீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: You with bright foreheads, see the way [his] waist
has close-set coral and pearls on the fine [waist] string of the Supreme Being
who runs, forcibly grasping and killing the one
who drags along the frenzied elephant with a black trunk
Come and see!
gloss: participial noun, present tense, masculine, singular, accusative
pronominalised noun, second person, plural, vocative

ta: வுந்தி யிருந்தவா காணீரே யொளியிழை யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: You with bright ornaments, see the quality of the supremely beautiful navel
of the child of Nanda who, like an elephant with a stick
being aloof toward the swarm of children who come [to play]
plays [by] himself. Come and see!
gloss: pronominalised noun, plural, second person, vocative

ta: வுதர மிருந்தவா காணீரே யொளிவளை யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: You with bright bangles, see the quality of the stomach
that was bound with an old rope
[when] the cowherdess deceived and detained [him]
being unable to rush [around], she fed from [her] sweet breast
the one has the colour of the thundering sea. Come and see!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person, accusative
pronominalised noun, second person, plural, vocative

ta: திருமார் பிருந்தவா காணீரே சேயிழை யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: You with beautiful ornaments, see the way the holy chest shines resplendently
with ornaments of brilliant, large gems [on] this child who
having been bound to a great big mortar
destroyed the two large Arjuna [trees]. Come and see!
gloss: pronominalised noun, plural, second person, vocative

ta: தோள்க ளிருந்தவா காணீரே சுரிகுழ லீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: You with spiraled curly hair, see the quality of the shoulders of he who
at [only] four or five months, went and destroyed the cart
by stretching out [his] leg [and] snatched away the precious life
of [her with] bright, crooked teeth. Come and see!
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, second person, plural, vocative

ta: கைத்தலங் கள்வந்து காணீரே கனங்குழை யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: You with golden earrings, come and see the palms of the hands
in which remain the conch and blood tipped discus
of the small child with the complexion of the blue lily in a high field
who is being raised by the kohl [lined] wide-eyed Yaśodā. Come and see!
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, plural, vocative

ta: கண்ட மிருந்தவா காணீரே காரிகை யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: Ladies, see the quality of the throat that swallowed heaven and earth whole
of the cowherd boy who was taken in and is being raised
as the son of the cowherdess whose curly hair
[is adorned with] flowers where bees abide. Come and see!
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, plural, vocative

ta: செந்தொண்டை வாய்வந்து காணீரே சேயிழை யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: Red-jewelled Ladies, come and see this red toṇṭai [fruit] mouth
that was zealously drunk in by the toṇṭai [fruit] mouths of cowherdesses
craving the nectar of [his] beautiful toṇṭai [fruit] mouth taking [him] up saying
“come our lion with the toṇṭai [fruit] mouth.” Come and see!
gloss: pronominalised noun, plural, second person, vocative

ta: மூக்கு மிரந்தவா காணீரே மொய்குழ லீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: Ladies with thick curls, see the quality of the form
eyes, mouth, teeth, and nose of this lord who
being seen by Yaśodā, [his] tongue is rubbed
with powdered turmeric and bathed. Come and see!
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, plural, vocative

ta: கண்க ளிருந்தவா காணீரே கனவளை யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: You with gold bangles, see the quality of the eyes of him who
Having previously come as the son of Vasudeva, occupying the earth
so that the agony of the immortals in heaven ended
grows so that the powerful Asuras are weakened. Come and see!
gloss: present tense, participial noun, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, second person, plural, vocative

ta: புருவ மிருந்தவா காணீரே பூண்முலை யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: You with jewelled breasts, see the quality of the eyebrows of him
who is the colour of a beautiful, bright, dark sapphire
who was begotten by Devakī, who is equal in beauty to Tiru
in order to save the whole world just when [he] reached the fullness of youth. Come and see!

ta: திண்ண மிருந்தவா காணீரே சேயிழை யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: You with red jewels, see the quality of the sturdiness
of these Makara earrings, beautiful in colour
of the child who, while joyfully eating, revealed that [he] had eaten
the lands, the mountains, the oceans, and the seven worlds. Come and see!

ta: னெற்றி யிருந்தவா காணீரே நேரிழை யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: Fine-jewelled Ladies, see the quality of the forehead of him
who is the Supreme Being, who, having grasped the women
who were playing, building sand houses with a small winnow and toy pot
with Myna birds on [their] forearms, runs off! Come and see!
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, third person, plural, accusative
pronominalised noun, plural, second person, vocative

ta: குழல்க ளிருந்தவா காணீரே குவிமுலை யீர்வந்து காணீரே
en: You round breasted [ladies], see the quality of the curls of him
who wanders herding the groups of young claves with a beautiful staff
of green gold in the palm of [his] hand [and] as a string of small bells
and anklets mingle and resound everywhere. Come and see!
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, vocative, second person, plural

en: Those who say [these] twenty-one [verses] that were spoken with love
by the scholar of southern Puttuvai about [his] sacred head to feet
that had been previously spoken [by] Yaśodā, she with curling hair full of bees
they will go and unite in Vaikunta
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, feminine, third person
participial noun, third person, imperfective aspect

ta: மாணிக் குறளனே தாலேலோ வையமள ந்தானே தாலேலோ
en: Brahmā tenderly sent to you a small, coloured cradle that was made with
superior gold, adorned with rubies [and] closely set with diamonds
You who are the brahmacārin Dwarf, tālēlō!
You who measured the earth, tālēlō!
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect
participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine, singular, vocative

ta: னுடையாய் அழேலழேல் தாலேலோ வுலக மளந்தானே தாலேலோ
en: O Master, Śiva, the one who holds the skull, who mounts the bull
sent a beautiful waist ornament that was strung [and] joined
in the middle of brilliant pomegranate flowers along with gold and sapphires
Master, do not cry, do not cry, tālēlō! You who measure the earth, tālēlō!
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, vocative, second person

ta: தந்துவ னாய்நின்றான் தாலேலோ தாமரைக் கண்ணனே தாலேலோ
en: Our Lord, Indra himself, having given the tinkling anklet
that possesses beauty for [your] beautiful lotus feet
[and] sandalwood for [your] beautiful, sacred chest
he stands nearby, tālēlō! You with lotus eyes, tālēlō!

ta: செங்கட் கருமுகிலே தாலேலோ தேவகி சிங்கமே தாலேலோ
en: The immortals there in heaven sent a right-spiraled conch
tinkling anklets for [your] red feet
bangles for [your] hands, a string, and waist chain
Black cloud, red-eyed [one], tālēlō! The lion of Devakī, tālēlō!

ta: தொழுதுவ னாய்நின்றான் தாலேலோ தூமணி வண்ணனே தாலேலோ
en: Vaiśravaṇa, generous and without fault, holds a beautiful necklace
[and] five beautiful weapons saying
“these are suitable for the sacred chest of he who is beautiful,”
he stands nearby, worshipping [you], tālēlō! Pearl-hued [Lord], tālēlō!
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

ta: சோதிச் சுடர்முடியாய் தாலேலோ சுந்தரத் தோளனே தாலேலோ
en: Varuṇa sent a necklace of brilliant pearls from the flooded sea
superior coral, and beautiful bangles
that are befitting [your] greatness
Crown of effulgent light, tālēlō! You with beautiful shoulders, tālēlō!
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect

ta: கோனே யழேலழேல் தாலேலோ குடந்தைக் கிடந்தானே தாலேலோ
en: The sacred lady [who sits] upon the lotus that is full of sweet juice
sent a garland of Kaṟpaka [flowers] from the abundant groves of heaven
and a handmade chaplet of fragrant tulasi that flourishes in the jungle
King, do not cry, do not cry, tālēlō! You who slept in Kuṭantai, tālēlō!
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine, singular, vocative

ta: நச்சு முலையுண்டாய் தாலேலோ நாராய ணாவழேல் தாலேலோ
en: Lady Earth sent “for Acyuta” knife of gold along with a belt
silk cloth, a golden bracelet, a sapphire head ornament
and golden flowers in a row for [your] bright feet
You who drank the poison breast, tālēlō! Nārāyaṇa, do not cry, tālēlō!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect, vocative

ta: ளையா வழேலழேல் தாலேலோ வரங்கத் தணையானே தாலேலோ
en: The female rider of the fierce stag stood nearby holding vermilion
kajal for [your] red, wide eyes
and tumeric with fragrant powder that is rubbed on [your] body
Master, do not cry, do not cry, tālēlō! You who recline in Araṅkam, tālēlō!
There is no affliction for those who master without deficiency
the words of the scholar of Putuvai who lives among brahmins of correct language
that the Cowherdess sang while rocking [to sleep] the kohl coloured
one who drank [from] the breast of the demoness who had come with lies
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Great young Moon, if there are eyes in your head
come here and behold the dancing of my son Govinda
who is covered in dust while the golden anklets tinkle
and, crawling along, the forehead ornament on his face sways to and fro
gloss: present tense, participial noun, masculine, singular

en: Big Moon, our Lord, my little lad, a sweet nectar to me
revealing [you] over and over with his little hands, he calls [you] by name
if you desire to dance the dance with him who is the colour of kohl
don’t hide in the clouds, come running joyfully!
Big Moon, revolving halo of light circling [the sky] spreading light everywhere
However much you do, you are no match [for] my son’s face
Without injuring the palms of the sage resident in Vēṇkaṭha
that summon you, come running quickly!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: He whose hands [hold] the discus opened [his] big eyes wide
sitting on my hip, [he] points out and reveals you, see!
If you know what is proper, Moon, do not deceive [him]
if you are not a sterile man who has not begotten children, come and see!
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: He calls you with immature young words
prattling indistinctly with trickling nectar on his beautiful lips
Big, bright Moon, if you leave as the beautiful Śrīdhara calls and calls
your ears are without holes
The eyes of him
whose broad hands hold the śārṅga bow and discus
along with a club
wishing to sleep, he keeps yawning
If [he] is not put to sleep, the breast milk that [he] drank
will not be digested, you see
Big Moon who remains in the sky, come running quickly!
gloss: present tense, third person, masculine, singular

en: Do not be contemptuous thinking, “he is an infant,”
this here is the boy who slept on the banyan leaf long ago
If he is angry, when [you] rise, he will leap up and grab [you]
Without disrespecting Māl, Big Moon, come running joyfully
Do not slight my young lion thinking, “he is small,” you see!
Go and ask Mahābali for news of [his] smallness
And if you take his smallness as a fault, you are the owner of your own affairs, you see!
Tall Māl calls you, Full Moon, [come] quickly!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
present tense, third person, masculine, singular

en: Our Lord with a large belly who, when [his] broad hands were full
devoured butter from the pot, see! He calls you
Taking up a discus, he will throw [it] at you, there is no doubt, see!
If you want to live, Big Moon, come running joyfully!
gloss: present tense, third person, masculine, singular

en: There is no affliction for those who are able to say all of these Tamil [verses]
that were written by Viṣṇu Cittaṉ, sage of bright Puttūr
with these words that were spoken that resemble those
spoken by Yaśodā, with koel [lined] wide eyes, for her son
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: You with the sapphire stomach which [contains] the world
that you created and consumed so that it would be saved
Supreme Being who has gently slept the yogic sleep
upon that banyan leaf for each of many successive aeons
You with a body [the colour] of khol with wide lotus eyes
having recalled that your chest is the refuge of the Red Lady
Lord, please dance one time for me so that [your] ears
[adorned with] Makara earrings abounding in riches, shine and shimmer
Battle bull of the cowherds, dance the Ceṅkīrai, please dance!
With the form of a murderous lion, you are the one who scoops out the blood
of the Asura’s body with [your] sharp claws so that [it] spurts out [and] shoots up
having intended for the truth to be grasped and so that his son would be liberated
When the Lord of the immortals above came greatly enraged
intending for those abundant black clouds to pour forth stones along with pebbles
you are the one who protected the cows with a mountain as an umbrella!
Lord, dance one time for me! Battle bull of the cowherds, dance the Ceṅkīrai, please dance!
gloss: imperfective aspect, second person, singular, participial noun, vocative
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular, participial noun, vocative

en: Our Lord, Meaning of the four Vedas
You who at one time became the mother of the four-faced one
[born upon] the good lotus in [your] navel!
You who, having stroked all the lands of the earth and the world of the stars
grew to expand even outside of that!
He is the one who, at that time that was appointed
came having conquered the elephant and seven bulls!
Hey! Dance one time for me! Battle bull of the cowherds, dance the Ceṅkīrai, please dance!
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, vocative, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, masculine, vocative, perfective aspect

en: You who drank that poison from the deceitful demoness’s breast
and overtuned the strong cart so that the celestials rejoiced!
My little calf of dark complexion who
intending to drop the hard, unripe fruit of the wood-apple tree in the forest
grasped a calf and threw it!
Elephant who goes into battle while shaking so that those [demons]
called Dhenuka, Mura, and valorious, cruel Naraka bend
dance one time for me! Fighting bull of the cowherds, dance the Ceṅkīrai, please dance!
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, vocative, perfective aspect
participial noun, third person, imperfective aspect

en: Having taken by the handful with trickery
[you] totally devoured the ghee that was kept by the good women
with long, curling hair, along with the curds
that measured [as high as] the churning rod
You who has great strength who opposed with thighs and hands
those who emerged from the identical twin Marutam [trees]!
So that [your] beautiful thick curls sway to and fro in front of [your] face
[with] young, pearl [like] teeth before becoming fully grown
O Father, dance one time for me!
Battle bull of the cowherds, dance the Ceṅkīrai, please dance!
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, neuter plural
perfective aspect, participial noun, third person, accusative
pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: You who takes the colour of the Kāya blossom!
You who has a complexion like a dark cloud!
O my beautiful child who practices the holy dance
on the head of Kāḷiya in the great pond in the forest!
You who plucked out the tusk of the tall, frenzied elephant!
You who has a pair of feet that dance
knowing [how to] wrestle, having destroyed without pause the wrestlers
who came in opposition [to you] to do battle!
O Cowherd, dance one time for me!
Fighting bull of the cowherds, dance the Ceṅkīrai, please dance!
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative

en: You who became the very powerful husband of Nappiṉai
—with curls of pure black, like the beautiful feathers of the peacock—
when, without swerving from the word of the strong cowherds
the seven good bulls perished for [her] sake
O my Father who, having driven a chariot alone, reunited with [their] mother
the children who were lost when [they] entered the great light
dance one time for me!
Battle bull of the cowherds, dance the Ceṅkīrai, please dance!
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, vocative, perfective aspect

en: So that the maidens who come, having grasped you to [their] hips
join together with you in their houses [and] their desires accomplished, rejoice
so that the eyes of those who see are refreshed
so that scholars come stumbling
having graced me who begot [you], You of eternal Kuṟuṅkuṭi
You of Veḷḷaṟai, O King of Cōlaimalai, surrounded by walls
O Nectar of Kaṇṇapuram, You who removes my suffering, please dance!
You who possesses the seven worlds, dance the Ceṅkīrai, please dance!
gloss: participial noun, neuter plural, perfective aspect
participial noun, plural, third person, perfective aspect
proper name, pronominalised noun, second person, vocative
proper name, pronominalised noun, second person, vocative
participial noun, imperfective aspect, second person, vocative
participial noun, singular, vocative, second person

en: So that campaka with bright sandal, ghee and curds
along with milk, and good camphor [with] lotus come emitting fragrance
so that [your] few teeth like tender white shoots glisten
between [your] red coral lips [like] beautiful and fragrant coral
so that the nectar of your ripe mouth splits, breaks off and falls over
in the midst of the beautiful five weapons [of you] with a blue colour
O Meaning of the Vedas that are suitable, please dance!
You who possesses the seven worlds, dance the Ceṅkīrai, please dance!
gloss: participial noun, singular, vocative, second person

en: So that the shining rings joined to [your] fingers like small petals
and the tinkling anklets to [your] red lotus feet
the gold cord that abides on [your] waist, the gold and sapphire
with flowers of the good pomegranate on [your] legs
the finger-ring, the coral bracelet, the auspicious five weapons
the arm band, earring, Makara, ear-studs, and forehead ornament
shine suitably, O King of our family, please dance!
You who possesses the seven worlds, dance the Ceṅkīrai, please dance!
gloss: participial noun, singular, vocative, second person

en: Those who are skillful in [reciting] these ten sweet song garlands of Tamil [verse]
that were spoken by the scholar of famed Putuvai
that are of a quality that is pleasing [like the words] of Yaśodā
the simple lady with the swan [like] gait, saying
“You who became the swan, the form of a fish, the man-lion, the dwarf, and the tortoise
O Leader of the cowherds, You who removes my suffering, please dance!
You who possesses the seven worlds, please dance the Ceṅkīrai, please dance!,”
they will obtain great joy [and] the praise of the eight regions of the world
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, vocative, perfective aspect
participial noun, imperfective aspect, second person, vocative
participial noun, singular, vocative, second person

ta: காணிகொண்ட கைகளால் சப்பாணி கருங்குழற் குட்டனே சப்பாணி
en: While [your] ruby anklets jingle, having adorned beads of gold
that were made with superior gold upon [your] waist
so that the pearls of [your] coral mouth shine
[clap] cappāṇi with the hands that long ago grasped the land [of Mahābali]
O child with black curls, [clap] cappāṇi!

ta: மன்னரை மேல்கொட்டாய் சப்பாணி மாயவ னேகொட்டாய் சப்பாணி
en: So that [your] belt of ruby bells along with a golden waist string
dances upon your waist while a single forehead ornament
hanging low, sways [to and fro], having remained upon my waist
drop down, clap cappāni upon the waist of the king of us cowherds! Māyavaṉ, clap cappāni!
My sapphire hued [child], clap cappāṇi upon the waist of your mother
so that [your] pearls shine in your ruby mouth, with shining gold leaf earrings above
like many gems and pearls inlayed in pleasing coral!
You whose hands [bear] the discus, [clap] cappāṇi!

ta: கோனிலா வக்கொட்டாய் சப்பாணி குடந்தைக் கிடந்தானே சப்பாணி
en: Having gone to the courtyard with white moonlight, having stood
calling, “O bright Moon in the sky, O Candrā, come to play!,”
clap cappāṇi so that the king of the cowherds
—who continuously praise you—
shines! You who reclines in Kuṭantai, [clap] cappāṇi!
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine, singular, vocative

ta: பட்டிக்கன் றேகொட்டாய் சப்பாணி பற்பநா பாகொட்டாய் சப்பாணி
en: O calf of the cattle stall who, having come
bringing [and] pressing mud and dust on [my] waist
[and] having entered inside unseen
ate the curds from the earthen vessel and the butter in the pot
clap cappāṇi! O you with the lotus navel, clap cappāṇi!

ta: தேருய்த்த கைகளால் சப்பாணி தேவகி சிங்கமே சப்பாணி
en: With the hands that led the chariot of the five long ago
so that the king who had prepared to rule the earth
—he who, not accepting the word of the father of the hundred
came to conduct battle—
perished, [clap] cappāṇi!
Lion of Devakī, [clap] cappāṇi!
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, third person

ta: சரந்தொட்ட கைகளால் சப்பாணி சார்ங்கவிற் கையனே சப்பாணி
en: With the hands that discharged arrows to agitate the ocean
that had remained hidden, so that the waves crashed
striking the hands that beseeched the deep ocean
that remained spread out [clap] cappāṇi!
You with the hands [that bear] the śārṅga bow, [clap] cappāṇi!

ta: நெருக்கிய கைகளால் சப்பாணி நேமியங் கையனே சப்பாணி
en: Having beseiged the roaring ocean with a group of monkeys
having built a bridge [across] the deep water
[clap] cappāṇi with the hands that assailed the demons of Laṅkā
with destructive arrows so that they perished!
You with the hands [that bear] the discus, [clap] cappāṇi!

ta: பிளந்திட்ட கைகளால் சப்பாணி பேய்முலை யுண்டானே சப்பாணி
en: [Clap] cappāṇi with the hands that
when [he] struck the post that had been measured and erected there
you who had grown in the form of a lion with sharp claws
dug out the heart of Hiraṇya, splitting the width of [his] bright chest
You who drank from the breast of the demon, [clap] cappāṇi!
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative
participial noun, singular, masculine, vocative, perfective aspect

ta: கடைந்திட்ட கைகளால் சப்பாணி கார்முகில் வண்ணனே சப்பாணி
en: With the hands that
the immortals having gathered, crowding the deep sea
fixed Mount Mandara as a churning rod, tied a rope around [it]
and churned [the sea] with Vasukī as a strong rope
[clap] cappāṇi! You with the complexion of a dark cloud, [clap] cappāṇi
The karma of those who speak with desire the ten cappāṇi [verses]
that were spoken with desire by the scholar of Villiputtūr
with gardens that bloom, emiting fragrance daily
about the king of the cowherds who appeared in order to grasp [his] servants
will depart
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person

en: Like an elephant that stands slowly and ambles along
while the stream of ichor that appears in three places oozes out
so that the hanging gold bells ring
[and] the chain of shackles [on his] trunk clink and rattle
will he [whose] hand [holds] the śārṅga bow
not come with a tottering walk with [his] pair of broad feet
so that the drum [like] bells on [his] waist cloth ring
[and his] tinkling anklets join in, jingling loudly?
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, imperfective aspect
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: Will Vāsudeva
he with the complexion of fitting dark sapphires
he who sleeps on Ananta
he who wears a tortoise necklace [and] a string of bones
not come with a tottering walk
while the tender shoot of his cool white tooth shines
on the surface of the mound of [his] smiling red coral mouth
resembling a beam of the small crescent moon
that appears on the tip of a branch in the middle of the red evening sky?
gloss: imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: The pipal leaf ornament that shines on a braid [around his waist]
along with [his] golden smallcloth
having become the streak of lightning, the white moon, and the surrounding halo
along with the gold necklace on [his] neck
[being] like a black cloud that shines with lightning
will Hṛṣīkeśa who shines in him not come with a tottering walk?
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, noun, singular
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: Having come laughing ‘ha ha ha’ [with nectar] flowing
like a pot of sugar cane [juice] when opened
my cloud-hued one with Śrī on his chest
who comes and stands before [me] giving [me] a kiss
having given the nectar of his mouth to me who begot him
he causes me to rejoice
Will he not come with a tottering walk on top of the heads of the enemies who strike him?
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, first person, singular, dative
causative, present tense, third person, singular
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: Like when the child [like] a big, good, white mountain, rumbling, runs swiftly ahead
[and] the child [like] a black mountain that follows after moves forward
the world consideratly praises Baladeva of unending fame
while his little brother runs after [him]
will the one who went to join [him] not come with a tottering walk?
gloss: participial noun, third person, neuter singular
participial noun, singular, masculine, imperfective aspect
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: Walking so that marks appear as if [he] drew here and there
with [his] two feet that became still [upon the earth]
having imprinted the soles of [his] feet with
the conch on one foot [and] the discus on the other foot
[he] pours down before and behind [himself]
a flood of delight that continuously spreads
will the father of Kāma
he with the complexion of the dark black ocean
come with a tottering walk?
gloss: imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: While [the nectar] continuously oozes, dribbles, and drips
from [his] vast red mouth like the small drops
that appear as dew when the expanding lotus blossom fully blooms
while the bells on [his] waist jingle
like the bells on the neck of the ferocious bull
will he who bears the Sarṅga bow
come with a tottering walk with [his] pair of broad feet
gloss: imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: Just as rivers move upon the side of a small, dark hill
as a string of bones hangs low, rising and falling
[and] moves side[-to-side] on [his] ornamented loins
[he] pours down [his grace] upon the human world
unknown when [he] came to stay with the form of a jewel [like] child
will Vāsudeva with complexion of a dark jewel come with a tottering walk?
gloss: imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: Like the one dark elephant calf that wallowed
having poured white dust upon [himself]
Trivikrama, having played in fine dust
sweats so that small spots appear
[his] small lotus feet with bright flower buds
fall without once feeling pain
will he come onto the cushion with cool buds with a tottering walk?
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, third person, noun, singular
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: While the glittering forehead ornament
shining on the sacred-water [like] face of Keśava, red-eyed Māl
like the disc of the moon on the rolling ocean
moves on every side
while the water that produces the fruit of the sacred water
that is greater than even the Ganges rising with waves of great water
trickles down in little drops from [his] small penis
will [he] come with a tottering walk?
gloss: imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: Those who master reciting [the verses] expounded with excellence
by the renowned Viṣṇu Cittaṉ of the Vēyars
about him with a black complexion
who was born in the clan of cowherds
who came with a tottering walk so that
[his] mother rejoices [and his] enemies perish
they will beget children who bow to the feet of the sapphire hued Māyaṉ
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, third person, neuter plural

en: He who came swiftly before me, having bound in place
the anklets and forehead ornament made of gold
running to my waist like a cloud made of lightening
while the noise that is natural to that [anklet] made a tinkling sound
Oh! Oh! My Lord has come, Oh! Oh!
As [your] hair comes to crowd around your coral mouth
like bees that drink the honey of the red lotus flower
coming with hands that hold the conch
bow, sword, club, and discus, Oh! Oh!
having come, fully embrace [me]! Oh! Oh!
He with the black complexion who
having assisted in the Bhārata [war]
as the messenger of the five [Pāṇḍavas]
entered the good pond where the serpent that spit poison reclined
[and] graciously lept on the hood of the cobra
so that [it] feared [him]! Oh! Oh!
Lord of the Cowherds, Oh! Oh!
You who pierced [her] oozing hump that day
so that [it] shrunk inside [and she] rose up
when [you] said, “give a little fragrant sandal to us,”
having understood, she annointed [your] holy body!
Oh! Oh! our Lord has come, Oh! Oh!
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, second person, singular

en: He who gazed hotly at the very deceitful Duryodhana
who, shining like the sun
while surrounded by kings with warrior’s anklets
saw you, began to depart, returned, and sat down! Oh! Oh!
He who bears the discus in his hand! Oh! Oh!
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative

en: Fighting impartially, you drove the chariot with equanimity
for the sake of Vijaya, [wearing] a fresh garland
in order to end the burdens of this earth
O He with big, dark eyes [and] a body that resembles a rain cloud!
Having come, embracing [me] fully, Oh! Oh!
Battle bull of the cowherds, Oh! Oh!
O He whose hand [bears] the discus
who poked with a bit of straw the eye of Śukra
who forbade the gift saying, “this is not proper,”
at the sacrifice of Māvali of very great fame, Oh! Oh!
He with the conch on his left side! Oh! Oh!
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: He with the flashing crown
who whirled the persistent Namuśi into the sky
when [he] said, “What is this deception? My father did not know
Take [your] previous form [and] measure [the earth]!”
Oh! Oh! Resident of Vēṅkaṭam! Oh! Oh!
He who filled [his] begging bowl when Śiva
with a crown of matted locks and garlands
[came] to beg for himself, saying
“O cloud-hued One, the oceans that can be seen
mountains, and all the seven worlds do not
assuage [the hunger] of [my] skull bowl,”
Oh! Oh! He with the mark on [His] chest! Oh! Oh!
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative

en: He who became that goose that day
when the great darkness that was thick surrounded
[and] shrouded the world
[and] the eternal four Vedas had completely vanished
so that the great darkness was afterward dispelled from this world
Oh! Oh! He who bestowed the precious Vedas! Oh! Oh!
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative

en: Those who constantly sing the words
of the scholar-king of Putuvai with storied, ornamented mansions
that were spoken by the cowherdess, saying
“Oh! Please come!”, to Nārāyaṇaṉ who stands before [His] devotees
will rule the high heavens
gloss: participial noun, third person, imperfective aspect
perfective aspect, participial noun, neuter singular

en: My little one, coming while droplets drip
like pearls that appear from the tip
of [His] ruby [red] penis
that grows between [two] balls
will embrace me [from] behind
Govinda will embrace me [from] behind
gloss: imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: Wearing tinkling anklets [and] a coral bracelet
putting bangles on [His] hands
[and] wearing a chain on [His] neck
my Kaṇṇaṉ, having come walking gracefully
with the collection of them
will embrace me [from] behind
my Lord will embrace me [from] behind
gloss: imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: [He] who appeared in order to ruin
the clan of the leader of the assembly
he who ruled the land
having not himself agreed to concede the great wealth
that had accumulated
comes, the Lord will embrace me [from] behind
The bull of the cowherds will me [from] behind
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, masculine, singular

en: He who, for the sake of Dhanañjaya who prostrated
[saying] “Nampi who holds the sword Nāntakam is the refuge,”
drove the solid, jewelled chariot of Vijaya
so that the kings upon the earth were terrified
will embrace me from behind
The king of celestials will embrace me from behind
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular

en: Wearing a leaf of bronze, playfully [coming] under a forest
of dark peacock feathers made of many eyes
while singing many songs and intoning ‘many years’
he who took the many worlds of old will embrace [me] from behind
Vāmana will embrace me from behind
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: He with auspicious features, holding an umbrella
as a unique brahmacāri, while the warriors watched
the one [Mahābali] who stood at the northern altar
who took the whole land will embrace [me] from behind
He who measured the earth will embrace me from behind
gloss: imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular
participial noun, singular, masculine, third person
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: The Lord who, having turned over the perforated mortar
[and] climbed atop it, devoured [all] the sweet milk
and the butter in pots so that [his] holy stomach was very full
comes, he will embrace me from behind
He with the discus will embrace me from behind
gloss: imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: Climbing the old sand hill so that the ancient assembly saw
delightedly dancing a dance, [and] singing a tune
with [his] flute while the men of the Vedas
who approached bow [to him and] immortals praise [him]
he will come and embrace me from behind
Our Lord will embrace me from behind
gloss: imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: Saying to [his] beloved
who desired the grove of Kaṟpaka trees in Indra’s garden
“I will give [it to you] now,”
[and] made it stand in [her] bright, moonlit courtyard
he who carried [it] will embrace me from behind
The King of celestials will embrace me from behind
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, third person
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular
imperfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: Those who master these ten tamiḻ [verses] that joyously grant
the words of the wide-bamboo-shouldered lady
the cowherdess who was embraced by the discus Lord from behind that day
by Viṭṭucittaṉ, begetting good children who flourish, they will rejoice
He with the conch that blows in praise on [his] left side
blowing the good bamboo [flute]
that messenger who had a hand in the Bhārata war
—when the ten villages were not obtained—
for the sake of the patient kings
who were ruined in the deceitful gambling [game]
he is making [the face of] a hobgoblin
Oh! He is making [the face of] a hobgoblin!
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, present tense
singular, masculine, third person, present tense

en: The red-eyed babbler who stood in the fore on a sturdy chariot
as Pārtha bent [his] bow so that the hundred perished
[and] so that the kings with shoulders that resemble mountains
warriors on chariots, and many others were ruined and perished
is making [the face of] a hobgoblin
Oh! He is making [the face of] a hobgoblin!
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, present tense
singular, masculine, third person, present tense

en: Entering the hot water, climbing the Cadamba tree
leaping and dancing on Kāḷiya’s fiery hood
so that [his] anklets rang out, blowing [his] bamboo flute
the cowherd who stood as the wonderous one
comes and is making [the face of] a hobgoblin
Oh! He is making [the face of] a hobgoblin
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
singular, masculine, third person, present tense
singular, masculine, third person, present tense

en: Being born in darkness, preventing the threat to the simple
strong cowherds, [and] overturning strong Kaṃsa
so that [he] died that day
the fearsome one who took our flowered silks comes
and is making [the face of] a hobgoblin
Oh! He is making [the face of] a hobgoblin!
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, present tense
singular, masculine, third person, present tense

en: Having shattered the cart that was yoked to an ox
being bound for stealing ghee, being beaten with a churning rope
by Nanda’s wife and trembling so that [he was] very agitated that day
he who was bound is making [the face of] a hobgoblin
Oh! He is making [the face of] a hobgoblin!
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, present tense
singular, masculine, third person, present tense

en: Having been born well to the Lady Devakī
with young, soft breasts [like] copper pots
Appaṉ who was placed in our village of cattle herds
who devoured the ghee, milk, and curds
comes and is making [the face of] a hobgoblin
Oh! He is making [the face of] a hobgoblin!
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, present tense
singular, masculine, third person, present tense

en: Did she take [him] in adoption? Or did she herself beget [him]?
The Lord—the young lion of Yaśodā, that woman of intellect
the murderous lion of the cowherds with black curls full of [flower] clusters—
came and is making [the face of] a hobgoblin
O Mother! He is making [the face of] a hobgoblin!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, feminine, third person
singular, masculine, third person, present tense
singular, masculine, third person, present tense

en: With the word of her with the hard hunch-back
[that swells like] breasts
having granted the tallest elephants upon the earth
horses, and [his] kingdom in all directions to Bharata
[and] settling in the harsh jungle
He with beautiful eyes is making [the face of] a hobgoblin
Oh! He is making [the face of] a hobgoblin!
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, present tense
singular, masculine, third person, present tense

en: The strong one who, riding a bird in order to assist
the elephant who was caught in the mouth of the sinful crocodile
crying aloud in pain and lifting [its] trunk in worship
while saying “my Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!,”
ended the affliction that was experienced there
he came and is making [the face of] a hobgoblin
Oh! He is making [the face of] a hobgoblin!
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, present tense
singular, masculine, third person, present tense

en: Those who master these ten appūcci songs
that are full of the words expound by Viṭṭucittaṉ
about the master of the bow that shot arrows
in order to [bring] ruin to the strong man’s Laṅkā
they will go and live permanently in Vaikunta

ta: அரவ ணையா யாய ரேறே யம்ம முண்ணத் துயிலெ ழாயே
யிரவு முண்ணா துறங்கி நீபோ யின்று முச்சி கொண்ட தாலோ
வுரவுங் காணேன் வயிற சைந்தாய் வனமு லைகள் சோர்ந்து பாயத்
திருவு டைய வாய்ம டுத்துத் திளைத்து தைத்துப் பருகி டாயே
en: You with a serpent for a bed! Bull among cowherds!
Rise from sleep to drink [my] breast milk
You went to sleep without eating [last] night
and today it is nearing noon, is it not?
I do not see [you] in motion, you with the rumbling belly
as [my milk] trickles, spreading [from my] beautiful breasts
[come and] drink, playing and kicking
suckle with [your] holy mouth!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, vocative, second person
perfective aspect, participial noun, second person, singular

ta: வைத்த நெய்யுங் காய்ந்த பாலும் வடித யிரும் நறுவெண் ணெயு
மித்த னையும் பெற்ர றியே னெம்பி ரான்நீ பிறந்த பின்னை
யெத்த னையுஞ் செய்யப் பெற்றா யேதுஞ் செய்யேன் கதம்ப டாதே
முத்த னைய முறுவல் செய்து மூக்கு றிஞ்சி முலையு ணாயே
en: After your birth, my Lord, obtaining even this much stored ghee
heated milk, strained curds, or fragrant butter, I do not know
You get to do whatever [you want], I do nothing
[Please], without being angry, showing [your] pearl-like teeth
and sniffling with [your] nose, drink [from my] breast!

ta: தந்தம் மக்க ளழுது சென்றால் தாய்மா ராவார் தரிக்க கில்லார்
வந்து நின்மேற் பூசல் செய்ய வாழ வல்ல வாசு தேவா
உந்தை யாருன் திறத்த ரல்ல ருன்னை நானொன் றுரப்ப மாட்டேன்
நந்த கோப னணிசி றுவா நான்சு ரந்த முலையு ணாயே
en: If their children go [about] crying
when their mothers who are unable to bear [it]
come to complain about you, you are able to thrive, O Vācudeva!
Your father cannot reveal you [and]
I am unable to be furious at you about [even] one thing
O little one, jewel of Nandagōpaṉ, drink from my swollen breasts!
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, participial noun

ta: கஞ்சன் றன்னாற் புணர்க்கப் பட்ட கள்ளச் சகடு கலக்க ழியப்
பஞ்சி யன்ன மெல்ல டியாற் பாய்ந்த போது நொந்தி டும்மென்
றஞ்சி னேன்கா ணமரர் கோவே யாயர் கூட்டத் தளவன் றாலோ
கஞ்ச னையுன் வஞ்ச னையால் வலைப்ப டுத்தாய் முலையு ணாயே
en: Look! I feared that you would suffer
when you attacked the treacherous cart
that had been created by Kaṃsa
with your tender, cotton-like feet so that it was shattered and ruined
King of immortals! You who caught Kaṃsa with your own deceit
there was no limit to the [fear of] the herder clan that day
Drink from [my] breast!
gloss: perfective aspect, second person, singular, participial noun

ta: தீய புந்திக் கஞ்ச னுன்மேற் சினமு டையன் சோர்வு பார்த்து
மாயந் தன்னால் வலைப்ப டுக்கில் வாழ கில்லேன் வாசு தேவா
தாயர் வாய்ச்சொல் கருமங் கண்டாய் சாற்றிச் சொன்னேன் போக வேண்டா
வாயர் பாடிக் கணிவி ளக்கே யமர்ந்து வந்தென் முலையு ணாயே
en: If evil minded Kaṃsa who has [great] anger toward you
Seeing weakness
Catches [you] through deceit
I would not be able to live, O Vāsudeva!
I have spoken to explain that you must regard
the words from the mouth of [your] mother
Jeweled lamp of the herder village, there is no need to go!
Come and stay, drink from my breast!

ta: மின்ன னைய நுண்ணி டையார் விரிகு ழல்மேல் நுழைந்த வண்டு
வின்னி சைக்கும் வில்லி புத்தூ ரினித மர்ந்தா யுன்னைக் கண்டா
ரென்ன நோன்பு நோற்றாள் கொலோ விவனைப் பெற்ற வயிறு டையா
ளென்னும் வார்த்தை யெய்து வித்த விருடீ கேசா முலையு ணாயே
en: Those who see you who abides sweetly in Villiputtūr where bees
who crawl on the loose locks of ladies with lightning thin waists
hum sweet [sounds]
ask ‘what penance has she with the womb that begot him endured?’
Hṛṣīkeśa, who causes [such] talk to occur, drink from [my] breast!
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, second person, singular
participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

ta: பெண்டிர் வாழ்வார் நின் னொப் பாரைப் பெறுது மென்னு மாசை யாலே
கண்ட வர்கள் போக்கொ ழிந்தார் கண்ணி ணையாற் கலக்க நோக்கி
வண்டு லாம்பூங் குழலி னாருன் வாய முத முண்ண வேண்டிக்
கொண்டு போவான் வந்து நின்றார் கோவிந் தாநீ முலையு ணாயே
en: The women who live to watch [you] with desire
saying “Let us obtain one like you,”
watching with bewilderment, with both eyes, they do no leave
Ladies with locks [full of] blossoms where bees wander
Wanting to drink the nectar of your lips
Come and stand [here] to reach and take [you]
Govinda! You [should] drink from [my] breast
gloss: participial noun, third person, imperfective aspect
participial noun, accusative, third person, imperfective aspect

ta: இரும லைபோ லெதிர்ந்த மல்ல ரிருவ ரங்க மெரிசெய் தாயுன்
திரும லிந்து திகழு மார்வு தேக்க வந்தென் னல்கு லேறி
யொருமு லையை வாய்ம டுத்தொ ருமு லையை நெருடிக் கொண்டு
விருமு லையும் முறைமு றையா யேங்கி யேங்கி யிருந்து ணாயே
en: You made the limbs burn of the two wrestlers
like huge mountains, who opposed [you]
Come, climb onto my hips to drink to fill up to [your] beautiful
sacred, shining chest, suckling one breast with [your] mouth
and taking and rubbing the other with [your] hands
each breast in turn, crying over and over, sit [and] drink!

ta: அங்க மலப் போத கத்தி லணிகொள் முத்தஞ் சிந்தி னாற்போற்
செங்க மலமு கம்வி யர்ப்பத் தீமை செய்திம் முற்றத் தூடே
யங்க மெல்லாம் புழுதி யாக வளைய வேண்டா வம்ம விம்ம
வங்க மரர்க் கமுத ளித்த வமரர் கோவே முலையுணாயே
en: Do not make mishchief such that your red lotus face sweats
Like beautiful pearls scatterd inside a lovely lotus bud
It’s unnecessary to wallow in this courtyard
so the all your limbs are [covered in] dust!
Alas! King of the celestials who at one time
granted nectar to the immortals so that they were full!
Drink from [my] breast!

ta: ஓட வோடக் கிண்கி ணிக ளொலிக்கு மோசைப் பாணி யாலே
பாடிப் பாடி வருகின் றாயைப் பற்ப நாப னென்றி ருந்தே
னாடி யாடி யசைந்த சைந்திட் டதனுக் கேற்ற கூத்தை யாடி
யோடி யோடிப் போய்வி டாதே யுத்த மாநீ முலையு ணாயே
en: I was thinking, “[He is] Padmanabha,” about you
who comes singing with songs and melodies
and ankle bells that jingle as you run
Supreme One! Dancing and dancing and [then] become exhausted
if [you] consider [doing] that
Do not leave and go off running and dancing [your] dance!
You [should] drink from [my] breast!
gloss: present tense, participial noun, second person, singular, accusative

en: Those who master the song of Paṭṭarpirāṉ
—he with the ancient fame that decorates the earth—
of Villiputtūr where the perfume of beautiful, dewy water lillies continuously wafts
with the words, “O Mādhava! Eat!”, of the cowherdess with high, beautiful breasts
they will obtain a mind that falls upon Red-eyed Māl who is beautiful with excellence
The father of you who possesses greatness
having gone [and] being delayed
there is no one to protect you from the cruel Kaṃsa
with power to battle
O Ocean-hued One, would [you] go alone
wandering everywhere?
O Crazy One who drank the milk from the breast of the demoness!
Kēcava! Dear One!
All the ladies from the cow-herd village have come
to pierce your ears [and] I have prepared the areca nut
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine, singular

en: Having adorned beautiful coral on [your] waist
while the bells on [your] blossom[-like] feet jingle
O Nārāyaṇā who is not separate from the minds
of those who approach and worship - Come here!
O Lord who is difficult to contemplate!
I will put the thread [through your] ear without [any] pain at all
These gold earrings are good for the eyes and are beautiful
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, neuter plural

en: I have brought the earrings[in the shape of] of the makara
that live in the vast ocean that bears the entire earth
[When] I put the thread in your ears [they will become] hot
I will give you whatever you want
O sprout of the cowherds, shining light who appeared
in this cowherd clan in order to save [them]
O husband of Śrī, creating madness in the hearts of the young cowherdessess
Come here!
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: These cowherding children, who have good qualities
have put diamond earrings that have a beautiful hue
filling their long ears so that they hang down
[but] you, O Govinda!, do not heed [my] words
If [you let me] put this very beautiful pair of earrings [in your ear]
I will give [you] sweet jack-fruit and
[my] breast well adorned with a golden powder to drink
Praise to you O Lord! Come here!
Even though saying, ‘praise to you, O Lord!’
you do not heed [my words], with curly haired women you go
clasping hands, and entwining in the kuravai
if you come here, O Nampi, would I take [it as] a virtue?
If you acquiesce to putting the thread [in your ear], O Lord!
I will give [you] big rice cakes again and again
O Viṣṇu, with black curls, adored by ladies with broad, bamboo shoulders
do come here!
You who cried so that all the heavens heard
I adoringly looked inside your mouth [and] seeing all the worlds
feared in my mind - I knew [then that you are] Madhusūdhana
There [will be] no wound whatsoever
[but] your ears will be injured
Sit patiently for just a moment, Nampi! Krsna!
My Dark Cloud! Ocean-hued One! Protector! Drink [from my] breast!
gloss: participial noun, singular, vocative, second person, perfective aspect

en: You who, running [wild] saying
“I don’t want [your] breast [or] anything else”
plucking the earrings from your ears and throwing [them]
grazed the cow herd and, joyfully raising a mountain
protected [them] from a shower of stones!
You broke the bow! O Trivikkrama!
O Lord of the holy cowherd village!
I gave up without causing the increase to your ear. It is my fault!
gloss: singular, second person, perfective aspect, participial noun
participial noun, singular, vocative, second person

en: Look, don’t say ‘It is my fault’!
While I consumed the earth
looking at me with [such] love
you caught and beat me
as everyone looked on, no?
Vamana Nampi, whose banner is the enemy
of the serpent in the strong anthill
your ears [will] close up
Lord who is the cure for all suffering
[let me] place the thread, I speak the truth!
Thinking the words of those who spoke [to you] to be truth
saying “you seized and ate the butter”
catching [my] hand, did you not tie me
to the edge of the mortar so that [they] see me?
Speaking and laughing about those deeds
if you are far, O Sridhara, your ears with close up
Please take the thread from my hand
[so that] the women standing here don’t laugh
gloss: participial noun, third person, imperfective aspect
participial noun, third person, neuter plural, perfective aspect

en: What harm is it to you and these women if my ears swell and burn?
Is it not distressing to me who, when it became intolerable
gave up, thinking “[it] hurts [his] head”?
Won’t you look as all the boys in the village wander [about]
having had their ears expanded
O Hṛṣīkēśa who, having overcome the ploughing bull
threw the young calf, O my Eye!
Mingling [with women] in order to please the eyes
looking everywhere
O sweet Lord, always in the thoughts of ladies
with curls with fragrant blossoms
O Our Nectar, I will give [you] ripe fruits to eat
[and] put just one earring in your ear without pain
O Padmanābha who kicked the cart so that the bamboo was destroyed!
Come here!
If, saying “come” and grabbing my hand
[you] forcefully place the earring
so that there is injury to my ear
what pain [will] you experience here?
[My] ears will hurt. I am unable [to bear it]
I have brought Jaumoon plum fruits. See them, O Nampi!
O Dāmodhara, who previously drank the milk
so that the deceitful woman died and lept to break the cart
Come here!
Those who master all twelve antāti [verses]
that were spoken along with the twelve names
without being satisfied
by the king of Putuvai, he with with ancient fame
that fills the earth
so that the words that were said about holy Māl
by Yaśodā with excellence
having desired to place the Makara earrings
making [his] long ears expand so that they hang low
shine, remaining in the mind
they are the slaves of Acyuta

ta: வெண்ணெ யளைந்த குணுங்கும் விளையாடு புழுதியுங் கொண்டு
திண்ணென விவ்விரா வுன்னைத் தேய்த்துக் கிடக்கநா னொட்டே
னெண்ணெய் புளிப்பழங் கொண்டிங் கெத்தனை போது மிருந்தேன்
நண்ண லரிய பிரானே நாரணா நீராட வாராய்
en: I certainly do not agree [to let] you go to sleep this night
rubbing [all over the bed] with the smell of cattle
mixed with butter and the dirt [you] played [in]
With the gingili oil and tamarind fruit, I will be here for however long
O Lord who is difficult to approach, O Narana, come to [take your] bath

ta: கன்றுக ளோடச் செவியிற் கட்டெறும் புபிடித் திட்டால்
தென்றிக் கெடுமாகில் வெண்ணெய் திரட்டி விழுங்குமா காண்பன்
நின்ற மராமரஞ் சாய்த்தாய் நீபிறந் ததிரு வோண
மின்றுநீ நீராட வேண்டு மெம்பிரா னோடாதே வாராய்
en: If [you] catch big black ants to put in the ears of the calves
so that they run away, if [they] are scattered and hurt
let’s see how [you] collect and gulp down butter [then]
You who bent the enduring cadamba tree
today is holy ōṇam, [when] you were born
you must bathe in water! Our Lord, come, don’t run away!
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, second person, singular

ta: பேய்ச்சி முலையுண்ணக் கண்டு பின்னையும் நில்லாதென் னெஞ்ச
மாய்ச்சிய ரெல்லாருங் கூடி யழைக்கவும் நான்முலை தந்தேன்
காய்ச்சின நீரொடு நெல்லி கடாரத்திற் பூரித்து வைத்தேன்
வாய்த்த புகழ்மணி வண்ணா மஞ்சன மாடநீ வாராய்
en: Seeing when [you] drank from the breast of the demoness
afterward, my heart not waiting, even though all the cowherdesses
had gathered together [and] cried out
I gave [you my] breast
I have filled a pot with gooseberries and boiled water
O Sapphire-hued lord with flourishing glory!
Come to bathe in [your] ceremonial bath

ta: கஞ்சன் புணர்ப்பினில் வந்த கடிய சகட முதைத்து
வஞ்சகப் பேய்மகள் துஞ்ச வாய்முலை வைத்த பிரானே
மஞ்சளுஞ் செங்கழு நீரின் வாசிகை யும்நாறு சாந்து
மஞ்சன முங்கொண்டு வைத்தே னழகனே நீராட வாராய்
en: O Lord, who, having kicked the cruel cart
that came as a contrivance of Kamsa
placed [your] mouth on the breast
of the deceiful demon woman so that she died
I have brought turmeric, a garland of red lilies
fragrant sandal paste and kohl
[My] beauty, come to bathe in water

ta: அப்பங் கலந்தசிற் றுண்டி யக்காரம் பாலிற் கலந்த
சொப்பட நான்சுட்டு வைத்தேன் தின்ன லுறுதியேல் நம்பி
செப்பிள மென்முலை யார்கள் சிறுபுறம் பேசிச் சிரிப்பர்
சொப்பட நீராட வேண்டுஞ் சோத்தம் பிரானிங்கே வாராய்
en: Nampi! If you are desirous of eating
I [have made] sweet pastry balls mixed with ricecakes
and sugar mixed in milk [and] kept [them] good and hot
Praiseworthy Lord! [You] need a thorough bathing in water
those [girls] with soft, young, copper-pot [like] breasts
will laugh and spread petty gossip [about you]. Come here!

ta: எண்ணெய்க் குடத்தை யுருட்டி யிளம்பிள்ளை கிள்ளி யெழுப்பிக்
கண்ணைப் புரட்டி விழித்துக் கழைகண்டு செய்யும் பரானே
யுண்ணக் கனிகள் தருவ னொலிகட லோதநீர் போலே
வண்ண மழகிய நம்பீ மஞ்சன மாடநீ வாராய்
en: Lord! [You] who imitates an elephant goad [i.e.causes mischief]
spinning the pots of gingili oil, waking and pinching young children
opening and rolling [your] eyes
Beautiful lord, you with a complexion
like the flooding water of the roaring sea
I will give you fruit to eat
Come take [your] ceremonial bath!

ta: கறந்தநற் பாலுந் தயிருங் கடைந்துறி மேல்வைத்த வெண்ணெய்
பிறந்தது வேமுத லாகப் பெற்றறி யேனெம்பி ரானே
சிறந்தநற் றாயலர் தூற்று மென்பத னாற்பிறர் முன்னே
மறந்து முரையாட மாட்டேன் மஞ்சன மாடநீ வாராய்
en: My lord! Since the first [day of your] birth
I do not know of churned butter placed in pots
nor of curds nor milk freshly milked
Even if I forget [myself] in front of others
because of their spreading gossip
about [your] eminent birth mother
I am not able to speak a word [of this]
Come take your ceremonial bath!

ta: கன்றினை வாலோலை கட்டிக் கனிக ளுதிர வெறிந்து
பின்றொடர்ந் தோடியோர் பாம்பைப் பிடித்துக்கொண் டாட்டினாய் போலும்
நின்றிறத் தேனல்லேன் நம்பி நீபிறந் ததிரு நன்னாள்
en: It seems, having tied palm leaves to the tail of a calf
and throwing [it] so that ripe fruits dropped [down]
you went running after a snake, and having caught [it]
danced [upon it’s head]
Nampi, I do not have your strength
[This] is the sacred day upon which you were born
You must bathe well in water, Nārāṇā!
Come [here], do not run away!

ta: பூணித் தொழுவினிற் புக்குப் புழுதி யளைந்தபொன் மேனி
காணப் பெரிது முகப்ப னாகிலுங் கண்டார் பழிப்பர்
நாணெத் தனையு மிலாதாய் நப்பின்னை காணிற் சிரிக்கும்
மாண்க்க மேயென் மணியே மஞ்சன மாடநீ வாராய்
en: I am very happy to see your golden body
after having entered the cattle stall and wallowing in dust
even if whoever [else] sees you will ridicule [you]
You have no shame at all!
If Nappiṉṉai sees [you], she will laugh
Ruby! My Jewel! Come take your ceremonial bath!
gloss: participial noun, third person, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, vocative, second person

ta: கார்மலி மேனி நிறத்துக் கண்ண பிரானை யுகந்து
வார்மலி கொங்கை யசோதை மஞ்சன மாட்டிய வாற்றைப்
பார்மலி தொல்புது வைக்கோன் பட்டர் பிரான்சொன்ன பாடல்
சீர்மலி செந்தமிழ் வல்லார் தீவினை யாது மிலரே
en: Those who master the refined Tamil, full of excellence
of [this] song, composed by Paṭṭarpirāṉ, king of ancient Putuvai
that spreads across the earth
about how Yaśodā, with plentiful, girdled breasts
having desired [to give a bath to] Lord Kṛṣṇa
with a bodily complexion abounding in darkness
made [him] take a ceremonial bath
for them, there will be no bad karma
Come to the husband of Pinnai, the one who reclines in Per
the sole cause, the first of the ancient celestials
the king who took in service our whole lineage, including me
Caw! Caw! Comb [his] curly locks!
Caw! Caw! Comb the curly locks of Madhava!
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person

en: Come so that the curly black hair of Kannan—
he who has the colour of the Kaya flower
he who broke the disguised cart and the marutu trees
the child who had previously drank from the breast of the demoness—
is immaculate
Caw! Caw! Comb [his] curly hair
Caw! Caw! Comb the curly hair of he with the colour of a pure jewel
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular

en: Come to Kaṇṇaṉ of the cowherders
the great lord of the celestials who
having devoured the butter
placed in swaying nets in robust pots
promplty went to sleep
Caw! Caw!Comb [his] curly hair
Caw! Caw!Comb the curly hair of him with the black cloud complexion
Come to the child
who, having seen he who came as a deceptive demon
with the form of a bird hunting in a waterhole
thinking ‘it is a bird’, quickly split [its] mouth
Caw! Caw!Comb [his] curly hair
Caw! Caw! Comb the curly hair of he who drank for the breast of the demon
Coming everyday to the divine head of the Supreme lord
who, while grazing the herd of calves
grabbed one calf and threw it for fruit
without running around, wandering about
talking about [all] the things that happened
Caw! Caw!Comb [his] curly hair
Caw! Caw! Comb the curly hair of the discus lord
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, third person, neuter plural
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Caw! Caw! Comb the curly hair of he who
having decided to destroy the indestructible kings
of the clans in the East
rooted them out in the blink of an eye with [his] discus
Caw! Caw! Comb the culry hair of Govinda
gloss: negative, participial noun, third person, accusative
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, accusative

en: Caw! Caw! Without wandering, running around
desiring to eat the balls of rice and water-boiled rice
that were left for the demons
Comb the curly hair that is black like the bee
that suits the beauty of the Lord of the heavenly celestials
Caw! Caw! Comb the culry hair of Māyavaṉ!
Having juiced a tamarind and poured [its juice] on the densely curled hair
of he who created the beautifyl four-faced [Brahmā]
on the shapely blossom that arose [from his] navel
Caw! Caw! Comb [his] curly hair with an ivory comb
Caw! Caw! Comb the curly hair of Dāmodara!
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: Caw! Caw! Having placed the golden head of him
who long ago measure the entirety of this world
so that, having witnessed [this], the wives of the king obtained joy
on a bed of flowers, comb [his] curly hair at the back
Caw! Caw! Comb the curly hair of he with a thousand names
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular

en: Those who praise the words of the scholar-king of Villiputtūr
with walls that touch the heavens
[about] the words of the herdess who cried
“Caw! Caw! Come! Comb the curly hair
full of bees of him with the dark complexion”
[so that] those who see [him] wouldn’t ridicule [him]
[grasping this] poem, they will not attain [bad] karma
gloss: participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

en: Bring a staff for the one who follows after the cow herd
raising his toy bow, having cut a stick from the hedge
wearing a leaf [as an] amulet on his broad neck
and, having bound the feathers of a peacock, placed it in the back
Bring a staff for the one with a complexion the colour of the sea
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, masculine, singular, dative

en: Bring a staff with good form
suitable for the broad hand, that holds the conch
of my son who plays, wandering everywhere
Koṅku, Kuṭantai, Kōṭṭiūr, and Pēr
Bring a staff smeared with vermilion
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, third person, neuter singular

en: Bring one staff for the little calf herder
running ahead so that his ringletted curls loosen
he who became angry and killed Kamsa who stood against [him]
he who, having persisted, split the mouth of the bird who came against [him]
Bring one staff for the god of gods
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: Bring one staff for grazing calves [to] him
who says only one thing and says just one word
who took a vow [to join] the Bhārata war
and went there to Duryodhana with a thick crown
Bring a staff to the one with a complexion the colour of the sea
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, imperfective aspect
participial noun, masculine, singular, first person, imperfective aspect
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, dative
pronominalised noun, neuter singular, third person

en: Bring a staff for the one who
incarnating on earth as a great messenger
due to [his] anger at having requested a single city
from Duryodhana and being denied
pledging [his] hand to the Bhārata war
drove a chariot for Pārtha
Bring a staff for the god of gods
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular, dative

en: Bring a staff for the beautiful Lord
who granted grace to Pārtha at a young age
He who [sleeps] on a banyan leaf and on a serpent bed
He who rests a long time in the blue sea
Bring a staff for the one who sleeps in Kuṭantai
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine, singular
participial noun, perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular, dative

en: Bring a staff swiftly so that
the cruel one, he with that knot of curly hair
who took one eye from the form that resided
on Citrakūṭa mountain, which glitters of gold
doesn’t take your eye next
Bring a staff for the sapphire hued prince
Bring a staff for the one with the lightning crown
who bent the shaft of the bow that is without an equal so that
the ten jewelled crowns of the king of Laṅkā fell all at once
for the sake of Sītā with the lightning[-thin] waist
Bring a staff for the one who damned the sea
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine, singular, dative

en: Bring a staff for the one with the necklace
that shines [like] lightning
who, having cut to pieces the head and arms
of the king of Laṅkā in the South
said to lord Vibhīṣaṇa with jewels that shine like lightning
“[Reign] such that my shining name reaches [the whole] kingdom.”
Bring a staff for the resident of Vēṅkaṭam
Those who master [these] ten Tamil [verses]
spoken harmoniously by the scholar of Villiputtūr
on the words, “Caw! Caw! Bring a staff for the prince!”
spoken by the Great Lady
will beget children [and] rejoice in this world

ta: ஆனிரை மேய்க்கநீ போதி யருமருந் தாவ தறியாய்
கானக மெல்லாம் திரிந்துன் கரிய திருமேனி வாட
பானையில் பாலைப் பருகிப் பற்றாதா ரெல்லாம் சிரிப்ப
தேனி லினிய பிரானே செண்பகப் பூச்சூட்ட வாராய்
en: Lord, sweet like honey
going to graze the cowherd, wandering the whole forest
so that your dark, holy body fades
and drinking milk [straight] from pots
while all [your] foes laugh
you do not know that [you] are [our] rare medicine
Come so that [I can] adorn [you] with Ceṇpaka blossoms!

ta: கருவுடை மேகங்கள் கண்டா லுன்னைக்கண் டாலொக்கும் கண்க
ளுருவுடை யாயுல கேழு முண்டாக வந்து பிறந்தாய்
திருவுடை யாள்மண வாளா திருவரங் கத்தே கிடந்தாய்
மருவி மணம்கமழ் கின்ற மல்லிகைப் பூச்சூட்ட வாராய்
en: If [my] eyes see a dark cloud it’s as if they see you
You who came, being born with a body to consume the seven worlds
You, bridegroom of Sītā, who sleeps in Holy Araṅkam
Come so that [I can] adorn [you] with jasmine blossoms that
strung together, emit [a sweet] fragrance!
gloss: participial noun, singular, vocative, second person
participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect
participial noun, second person, perfective aspect

ta: மச்சொடு மாளிகை யேறி மாதர்கள் தம்மிடம் புக்கு
கச்சொடு பட்டைக் கிழித்துக் காம்பு துகிலவை கீறி
நிச்சலும் தீமைகள் செய்வாய் நீள்திரு வேங்கடத் தெந்தாய்
பச்சைத் தமனகத் தோடு பாதிரிப் பூச்சூட்ட வாராய்
en: You are constantly up to no good
climbing the upper story of the mansions
entering the apartments of the ladies
tearing at the lace borders of [their] girdles
and rending those fine, silk clothes
My father of high, holy Vēṅkaṭam!
Come so that [I can] adorn [you] with verdant southernwood
and trumpet flower blossoms

ta: தெருவின் கணின்றிள வாய்ச்சி மார்களைத் தீமைசெய் யாதே
மருவுந் தமனக மும்சீர் மாலை மணம்கமழ் கின்ற
புருவம் கருங்குழல் நெற்றி பொலிந்த முகிற்கன்று போலே
யுருவம ழகிய நம்பீ யுகந்திவை சூட்டநீ வாராய்
en: Don’t stand in the street doing harm to the young herdesses
Like a cloud[-coloured] calf whose forehead is rich
with fragrant eyebrows and curly black hair
beautiful, shapely Prince!
Come joyfully so that [I can] adorn you
with these beautiful garlands of marjoram and
trumpet flower which emit a [sweet] fragrance

ta: புள்ளினை வாய்பிளந் திட்டாய் பொருகரி யின்கொம்பொ சித்தாய்
கள்ளவ ரக்கியை மூக்கொடு காவல னைத்தலை கொண்டா
யள்ளிநீ வெண்ணெய் விழுங்க வஞ்சா தடியே னடித்தேன்
தெள்ளிய நீரி லெழுந்த செங்கழு நீர்சூட்ட வாராய்
en: You who split the bird’s mouth!
You who snapped the war elephant’s tusk!
You who took the nose of the deceptive demoness
and the head of [her] protector!
[And yet,] when you scooped up and devoured the butter
I, your servant, beat you without fear
Come, so that [I can] adorn [you] with the
red waterlily that grows in the clear water!
gloss: participial noun, singular, vocative, second person, perfective aspect
participial noun, second person, perfective aspect, vocative

ta: எருதுக ளோடு பொருதி யேதுமு லோபாய்கா னம்பி
கருதிய தீமைகள் செய்து கஞ்சனைக் கால்கொடு பாய்ந்தாய்
தெருவின்கண் தீமைகள் செய்து சிக்கென மல்லர்க ளோடு
பொருது வருகின்ற பொன்னே புன்னைப்பூச் சூட்ட வாராய்
en: Prince! Look! Since fighting the oxen
you want for nothing at all
You who, causing the mischief [you] intended
lept [and grabbed] Kaṃsa by the leg
Golden one who, creating mischief in the streets
came along tenaciously to fight the wrestlers
Come so that [I can] adorn [you] with Puṉṉai blossoms!

ta: குடங்க ளெடுத்தேற விட்டுக் கூத்தாட வல்லவெங் கோவே
மடங்கொள் மதிமுகத் தாரை மால்செய்ய வல்லவென் மைந்தா
விடந்திட் டிரணியன் நெஞ்சை யிருபிள வாகமுன் கீண்டாய்
குடந்தைக் கிடந்தவெங் கோவே குருக்கத்திப் பூச்சூட்ட வாராய்
en: Our King, able to dance a dance upon pots raised high!
My son, able to trick the moon-faced ladies!
You who long ago cleaved in two pieces and dug out Hiranya’s heart
Our king who sleeps in Kuṭantai
come so that [I can] adorn [you] with Kurukkatti blossoms!
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect

ta: சீமாலி கனவ னோடு தோழமை கொள்ளவும் வல்லாய்
சாமா றவனைநீ யெண்ணிச் சக்கரத் தால்தலை கொண்டா
யாமா றறியும் பிரானே யணியரங் கத்தே கிடந்தா
யேமாற் றமென்னைத் தவிர்த்தா யிருவாட்சிப் பூச்சூட்ட வாராய்
en: Even though you were able to make friends with Śrī Mālika
Having considered the [best] way for him to die
you took his head with [your] discus
Lord who knows the future, you dispelled my confusion!
You who sleeps in beautiful Araṅkam
come so that [I can] adorn [you] with jasmine blossoms!
gloss: participial noun, second person, perfective aspect
perfective aspect, participial noun, second person, singular

ta: அண்டத் தமரர்கள் சூழ வத்தாணி யுள்ளங்கி ருந்தாய்
தொண்டர்கள் நெஞ்சி லுறைவாய் தூமல ராள்மண வாளா
உண்டிட் டுலகினை யேழு மோரா லிலையில் துயில் கொண்டாய்
கண்டுநா னுன்னை யுகக்கக் கருமுகைப் பூச்சூட்ட வாராய்
en: You sat there in the assembly hall
surrounded by heavenly celestials
You dwell in the hearts of servants
Oh Bridegroom of the pure Lotus Lady!
You slept on a banyan leaf having consumed the 7 worlds
So that I may rejoice in seeing you
come so the [I can] adorn [you] with Jasmine blossoms

ta: செண்பக மல்லிகை யோடு செங்கழு நீரிரு வாட்சி
யெண்பகர் பூவும் கொணர்ந்தே னின்றிவை சூட்டவா வென்று
மண்பகர் கொண்டானை யாய்ச்சி மகிழ்ந்துரை செய்தவிம் மாலை
பண்பகர் வில்லிபுத் தூர்க்கோன் பட்டர் பிரான்சொன்ன பத்தே
en: This garland of ten [verses] were spoken by Paṭṭarpirāṉ
king of Villiputtūr where melodies are uttered
made of the joyful words of the herdess
about him who took and moved the earth saying
“Come, so that [I can] adorn [you] with these today
I’ve brought a number of blossoms
such as the red water lily and Tuscan jasmine
along with the Champaka and Himalayan jasmine”

ta: இந்திர னோடு பிரமன் ஈச னிமைய வரெல்லாம்
மந்திர மாமலர் கொண்டு மறைந்துவ ராய்வந்து நின்றார்
சந்திரன் மாளிகை சேரும் சதிரர்கள் வெள்ளறை நின்றா
யந்தியம் போதிது வாகும் அழகனே காப்பிட வாராய்
en: Brahmā, Īśa, and all the [other] celestials
along with Indra
came, bringing the great flowers
[and] mantras and stood hidden nearby
You who stands in Veḷḷaṟai where clever men
are gathered in mansions [touched] by the moon!
Beauty! It is the beautiful time of twilight
come so that [I can] fasten a kāppu
gloss: participial noun, plural, third person, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect

ta: கன்றுக ளில்லம் புகுந்து கதறுகின் றபசு வெல்லாம்
நின்றொழிந் தேனுன்னைக் கூவி நேசமே லொன்று மிலாதாய்
மன்றில்நில் லேலந்திப் போது மதிள்திரு வெள்ளறை நின்றாய்
நன்றுகண் டாயென்தன் சொல்லு நானுன்னைக் காப்பிட வாராய்
en: I left all the cows bellowing to enter the calf shed
calling out to you, who has no heart
Do not stand in the crossroad at twilight
you who stands in walled holy Veḷḷaṟai!
What I say is right, you see!
Come, so that I [can] fasten you with a Kāppu
gloss: participial noun, singular, vocative, second person
participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect

ta: செப்போது மென்முலை யார்கள் சிறுசோறு மில்லும் சிதைத்திட்டு
அப்போது நானுரப் பப்போ யடிசிலு முண்டிலை யாள்வாய்
முப்போதும் வானவ ரேத்தும் முனிவர்கள் வெள்ளறை நின்றா
யிப்போது நானொன்றும் செய்யே னெம்பிரான் காப்பிட வாராய்
en: Supreme Lord! When, having destroyed the little [toy] rice [dishes]
and [sand] houses of the [girls] with soft copper pot-like breast
I became angry [and] you wouldn’t eat any food!
You who stands in Veḷḷaṟai with sages
who praise the gods three times [daily]
My Lord, I won’t do anything this time
Come so that [I can] fasten a kāppu!
gloss: second person, imperfective aspect, participial noun, vocative
participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect, vocative

ta: கண்ணில் மணல்கொடு தூவிக் காலினால் பாய்ந்தனை யென்றென்று
எண்ணரும் பிள்ளைகள் வந்திட் டிவரால் முறைப்படு கின்றார்
கண்ணனே வெள்ளறை நின்றாய் கண்டாரோ டேதீமை செய்வாய்
வண்ணமே வேலை யதொப்பாய் வள்ளலே காப்பிட வாராய்
en: Kaṇṇaṉ! Countless children come to complain
saying again and again that you pounce with [your] feet
thrashing about and scattering sand in [their] eyes
You who does mischief with [all] who see [you]!
You who stands in Veḷḷaṟai! Liberal One!
You who resembles the colour of the sea
Come so that [I can] fasten a Kāppu!
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect, vocative
participial noun, perfective aspect, third person, sociative
imperfective aspect, participial noun, second person, vocative
participial noun, singular, second person, imperfective aspect, vocative

ta: பல்லாயி ரவரிவ் வூரில் பிள்ளைகள் தீமைகள் செய்வார்
எல்லாமுன் மேலன்றிப் போகா தெம்பிரா னீயிங்கே வாராய்
நல்லார்கள் வெள்ளறை நின்றாய் ஞானச்சு டரேயுன் மேனி
சொல்லா ரவாழ்த்தி நின்றேத்திச் சொப்படக் காப்பிட வாராய்
en: In this town there are many thousands of children
doing mischief
But none of them will be attributed
[to anyone] but you, my lord. Come here!
You who stands in veḷḷaṟai where the good people [reside]!
Light of Knowledge!
Come so that [I can] neatly fasten a Kāppu
while [I] am continually praising and blessing your body with words
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect, vocative

ta: கஞ்சங்க றுக்கொண்டு நின்மேல் கருநிறச் செம்மயிர்ப் பேயை
வஞ்சிப்ப தற்கு விடுத்தா னென்பதோர் வார்த்தை யுமுண்டு
மஞ்சுத வழ்மணி மாட மதிள்திரு வெள்ளறை நின்றா
யஞ்சுவன் நீயங்கு நிற்க வழகனே காப்பிட வாராய்
en: That raging Kaṃsa dispatched a black complexioned
red haired demoness to deceive you is all the talk
You who stands in holy walled Veḷḷaṟai
with jewelled mansions crawling with clouds!
Beauty! I am afraid when you stand there
come so that [I can] fasten a Kāppu
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect, vocative

ta: கள்ளச் சகடும் மருதும் கலக்கழி யவுதை செய்த
பிள்ளை யரசேநீ பேயைப் பிடித்து முலையுண் டபின்னை
யுள்ளவா றொன்று மறியேன் ஒளியுடை வெள்ளறை நின்றாய்
பள்ளிகொள் போதிது வாகும் பரமனே காப்பிட வாராய்
en: Boy King! You who violently kicked the deceptive cart
and marutu [trees] to destroy [them]
Then seized the demoness and drank from [her] breast
I do not know how [you do this]
You who stands in radiant Veḷḷaṟai!
Supreme One! It is time for bed
Come so that [I can] fasten a Kāppu!
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect, vocative

ta: இன்ப மதனை யுயர்த்தா யிமையவர்க் கென்று மரியாய்
கும்பக் களிறட்ட கோவே கொடுங்கஞ்சன் நெஞ்சினிற் கூற்றே
செம்பொன் மதிள்வெள் ளறையாய் செல்வத்தி னால்வளர் பிள்ளாய்
கம்பக் கபாலிகா ணங்குக் கடிதோடிக் காப்பிட வாராய்
en: You who elevate joy!
You who are eternally eminent to celestials!
King who killed the foreheaded elephant!
Death to the heart of cruel Kaṃsa!
You of red-gold walled Veḷḷaṟai!
Child raised with wealth!
See the trembling Kapāli [monk] there!
Come, run swiftly so that [I can] fasten a Kāppu
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect, vocative
pronominalised noun, singular, vocative, second person
pronominalised noun, proper name, second person, singular, vocative

ta: இருக்கொடு நீர்சங்கில் கொண்டிட் டெழில்மறை யோர்வந்து நின்றார்
தருக்கேல்நம் பிசந்தி நின்று தாய்சொல்லுக் கொள்ளாய் சிலநாள்
திருக்காப்பு நானுன்னைச் சாத்தத் தேசுடை வெள்ளறை நின்றாய்
உருக்காட்டு மந்தி விளக்கின் றொளிகொள்ள வேற்றுகேன் வாராய்
en: Eminent Vedic scholars come
bearing water in a conch along with the Ṛg Veda and stay
Don’t be arrogant, [little] Prince!
Standing at the crossroads
adhere to the words of [your] mother for a few [more] days!
You who stands in lustrous Veḷḷaṟai
I will increase the light of the evening lamp that shows [your] form
Come so that I [can] adorn you with the holy Kāppu
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect, vocative

ta: போதமர் செல்வக் கொழுந்து புணர்திரு வெள்ளறை யானை
மாதர்க்கு யர்ந்த யசோதை மகன்தன்னைக் காப்பிட்ட மாற்றம்
வேதப் பயன்கொள்ள வல்ல விட்டுசித் தன்சொன்ன மாலை
பாதப் பயன்கொள்ள வல்ல பத்தருள் ளார்வினை போமே
en: The karma of those who are devotees
who are able to reap the fruit
