of the stanzas of [this] garland [of verses]
spoken by Viṣṇucitta who was able to reap the fruit of the Vedas
with the words about fastening the Kāppu
to the son of Yaśodā, superior among women
him of holy Veḷḷaṟai joined
to the tender shoot of wealth [Śrī] resembling a lotus bud
will depart
gloss: proper name, pronominalised noun, masculine, singular, accusative

en: We cannot prevent the malicious habits of Lord Kaṇṇa who
having devoured the butter
threw the empty pots on the stone [floor] to hear the sound
Restrain your son!
In house after house, he is able to commit such wickedness
as if pouring tamarind [juice] in a wound
Yaśodā, [you] have a son who has an excellent eye
My Lady, call your son!
Come! Come! Please come here!
Prince Vāmaṉa! Please come here!
Prince Kākutstha, with [your] black curls
red lips, and face, please come here!
Ladies! [Even] now, to me he is precious
Kohl coloured [Lord]! I cannot bear it
when those in the neighbourhood spew scorn
Ah! Come here to poor me!
gloss: pronominalised noun, first person, singular, dative

en: There is no one to stop the wicked ways
of this holy child, this radiant boy
Having drunk [all] the butter in the pots
that had been left to melt
he continued going about throwing and breaking [them]
The wrong done to those in the neighbourhood
is this justice Yaśodā?
Call your son to come! O Madhusūdana! He won’t let us be!
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect
participial noun, third person, perfective aspect
imperfective aspect, third person, noun, singular

en: Cloud- coloured One, come here!
Child of the temple, come here!
Divine Nāraṇā who lay in Tiruppēr
surrounded by clear waves, come here!
When [he] ran inside saying
“I have [already] eaten food,”
the herdess, seeing him, goes and lifts [him up]
this is the lesson learned by Kaṇṇapirāṉ!
As my daughter, with many bangles
placed fresh milk upon the fire
I went next door to ask for coal
and stood there talking for for just a minute
The prince of Śālagrāma [in the meantime]
went around tipping over and drinking [the milk]
My lady, Yaśodā with sweet words like pressed sugar-cane
call your son!
You know [you should] come!
You know [you should] come here!
You know [you should] come
without saying “I’m not coming!”
I cannot listen to anything that was said
by the neighbours when they say anything
You’re just a curious kid, arent you?
You who raised a mountain!
Dancer who danced with pots!
The meaning of the Vedas!
My Vēṅkaṭa [Lord]! Sage! Come here!
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, vocative
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, vocative, third person

en: I prepared sugary treats made of red paddy rice
and green gram, along with fragrant ghee and milk
for the twelve [days] of the holy Ōṇam [festival]
[But] I have known the nature of this child a long time
He went about devouring everything
saying “I want more than this.”
My Lady, Yaśodā! Call your son to yourself
These are only a few [of the things he’s done]
Keśava! Come here!
Come here without saying “I can’t!”
Don’t you play in the houses of unloving people!
Stay away from the places where slave women
and servants say terrible things
Considering the words of [your] mother
is your dharma, Dāmōdara! Come here!
Having placed sugary balls of sweetmeat, rice cakes
and balls of black sesame in a pot
[and] having stored [them], I left thinking “[it’s in] my house”
[But] he entered and went around eating them
Later, entering my house [again]
seeing the hanging pots, he investigates the shining light butter
Yaśodā, My lady! Call your son!
These are only a few [of the things he’s done]
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect
present tense, masculine, singular, third person

en: My Lady! When we speak [to you] you rise [like] a queen
[But] your son is deceptive!
Entering [my] house and calling my daughter
he steals the bangle [right] from [her] arm
gives that bangle to a girl there who was bringing [fruit]
from the grove to sell
takes [her] good plum fruits, and laughs saying “it wasn’t me!”
gloss: present tense, third person, masculine, singular

en: Those who are able to dance
singing these songs of Viṭṭucittaṉ, Lord of scholars
[about] all the playful things he did long ago
—He of Araṅkam in the south where the Kāviri river flows
surrounded by groves that buzz with revelling bees—
being servants of Govinda
they will stand as lamps for all the eight directions
with their pairs of feet upon my head
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Having thrown mud at us who were playing at the river
And stealing our bangles and fine clothes
He entered [his] house running swiftly like the wind
Because of him who won’t give [us] an answer
now we’re at our end
Because of him who won’t tell us where [our] bangles are
now we’re at our end
gloss: participial noun, plural, accusative, first person
negative, participial noun, masculine, singular, instrumental
negative, participial noun, masculine, singular, instrumental

en: While those of the eight directions
bow and worship and priase [him]
as [his] earrings and curls and necklace [all] hang low
He steals the fine clothes of those with flowered curls laden with bees
Because of him in the tree that touches the sky
now we’re at our end
Because of him who won’t give us what we want
now we’re at our end
gloss: participial noun, third person, neuter plural
negative, participial noun, masculine, singular, instrumental

en: Having agitated the broad lotus pond
Grasping and pulling at the tail of the venemous snake
He lept up atop [it’s] head with hoods spread
Because of he who moved [his] body
now we’re at our end
Because of he who stood atop [the snake’s] head
now we’re at our end
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, instrumental
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, instrumental

en: With the huge, broad arms that threw Dhenuka
onto the palm-fruit, destroying [his] life
[he] blocked the rains that came
as dispatched by the king of celestials [Indra]
Because of him who protected the cow herd
now we are at our end
Because of he who took [them] to save them
now we are at our end
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, instrumental
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, instrumental

en: He devoured a mix of curds and milk
from the village of the herdess
And when she returned, the lady with broad bamboo arms
saw him eating a handful
and caught him so that he couldn’t take the butter
Because of him who sat there eating rice
now we’re at our end
Because of him who was beaten and cried
now we’re at our end
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, third person
participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine, singular, instrumental
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, instrumental

en: As a young boy, with a fitful, staggering gait
seeing that which dwelt in her heart of hearts
he sucked the drop of life from the breast
of the demoness who came through deception
Because of him, now we’re at our end
Because of he who was fully bound
now we’re at our end
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, instrumental
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, instrumental

en: Having gone to Māvali sacrifice in the form of a dwarf
begging, “give [me] three steps”
he placed one foot [and took] the whole earth
[and with] the second foot on that [he took everything]
Because of him who placed his stretched out foot
now we’re at our end
Because of him who measure the earth
now we’re at our end
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, instrumental
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, instrumental

en: Having been caught in the crocodile’s trap
in a huge, wide pool with cool water-lilies and screw-pine
As the lord of celestials, he ended the suffering
of the elephant who was experiencing [such] trouble
Because of him who himself took on the service with [his] discus
now we’re at our end
Because of him who granted grace to that [elephant]
now we’re at our end
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine, singular, instrumental
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, instrumental

en: Like a rain cloud high in the sky
grazing through the forest everywhere
Rejoicing in play, as a boar he dug up this earth
Because of him who put it [the earth] in place
now we’re at our end
Because of him who dug up the earth
now we’re at our end
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, instrumental
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, instrumental

en: For those who master these words here by the scholar king of Putuvai
about the regularly occurring complaints of those there
the good girls coming to Yaśodā
about the beautiful lotus eyed boy
there will be no suffering

ta: தன்னே ராயிரம் பிள்ளை களோடு தளர்நடை யிட்டு வருவான்
பொன்னேய் நெய்யொடு பாலமு துண்டொரு புள்ளுவன் பொய்யே தவழும்
மின்னேர் நுண்ணிடை வஞ்ச மகள்கொங்கை துஞ்சவாய் வைத்த பிரானே
அன்னே யுன்னை யறிந்துகொண் டேனுனக் கஞ்சுவ னம்மம் தரவே
en: You who come with a thousand childring in tow
growing weary with with [each] step
Lord, who creeps [like] a theif [full of] lies
consuming the milk
along with the golden ghee as ambrosia
you placed your mouth on the breast of the deceitful lady
with the lightning-like thin waist so that she died
Alas! I have come to know you
[and] I am afraid to give you [my] breast milk!
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, imperfective aspect, vocative

ta: பொன்போல் மஞ்சன மாட்டி யமுதூட்டிப் போனேன் வருமள விப்பால்
வன்பா ரச்சக டமிறச் சாடி வடக்கில கம்புக் கிருந்து
மின்போல் நுண்ணிடை யாலொரு கன்னியை வேற்றுரு வம்செய்து வைத்த
அன்பா வுன்னை யறிந்துகொண் டேனுனக் கஞ்சுவ னம்மம் தரவே
en: Having bathed [you] in a radiant cerimonial bath
and fed you ambrosia, I left
By the time I came back, [you] had beaten the strong
heavy cart so that it broke
and entered the house to the north
[My] Love! Who [forever] altered the body
of the maiden with the lightning-like thin waist
I have come to know you
[and] I am afraid to give you [my] breast milk

ta: கும்மா யத்தொடு வெண்ணெய் விழுங்கிக் குடத்தயிர் சாய்த்துப் பருகி
பொய்ம்மா யமரு தான வசுரரைப் பொன்றுவித் தின்றுநீ வந்தாய்
இம்மா யம்வல்ல பிள்ளைநம் பீயுன்னை யென்மக னேயென்பர் நின்றார்
அம்மா வுன்னை யறிந்துகொண் டேனுனக் கஞ்சுவ னம்மம் தரவே
en: Devouring the butter along with the well-cooked dahl
tipping over and drinking the curd in pots
Now you come [along] killing the demon who became
a Marutu tree through deception and illusion
[my] boy prince skilled in illusion!
There are those who stand [here] saying you are my son
Alas! I have come to know you
[and] I am afraid to give you [my] breast milk
gloss: participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

ta: மையார் கண்மட வாய்ச்சியர் மக்களை மையன்மை செய்தவர் பின்போய்
கொய்யார் பூந்துகில் பற்றித் தனிநின்று குற்றம் பலபல செய்தாய்
பொய்யா வுன்னைப் புறம்பல பேசுவ புத்தகத் துக்குள கேட்டேன்
ஐயா வுன்னை யறிந்துகொண் டேனுனக் கஞ்சுவ னம்மம் தரவே
en: Infatuating the simple herding ladies with kohl-full eyes
[you] follow after them plucking and grabbing
at their beautiful flowered saris
[but] remaining alone, you commit more and more offences
Liar! I have heard so much slanderous talk about you
it could be a book!
Lord! I have come to know you
[and] I am afraid to give you [my] breast

ta: முப்போ தும்கடைந் தீண்டிய வெண்ணெயி னோடு தயிரும் விழுங்கி
கப்பா லாயர்கள் காவிற் கொணர்ந்த கலத்தொடு சாய்த்துப் பருகி
மெய்ப்பா லுண்டழு பிள்ளைகள் போலநீ விம்மிவிம் மியழு கின்ற
அப்பா வுன்னை யறிந்துகொண் டேனுனக் கஞ்சுவ னம்மம் தரவே
en: Lord who, devouring the curds and butter
that [I had] gathered, having churning [it] three times
And tipping and drinking the pots that had been brought
carried by herders on a pole
is sobing and sobing
wailing like crying children drinking breast milk!
I have come to know you
[and] I am afraid to give you [my] breast milk

ta: கரும்பார் நீள்வயல் காய்கதிர்ச் செந்நெலைக் கற்றா நிறைமண்டித் தின்ன
விரும்பாக் கன்றொன்று கொண்டு விளங்கனி வீழ வெறிந்த பிரானே
சுரும்பார் மென்குழல் கன்னி யொருத்திக்குச் சூழ்வலை வைத்துத் திரியும்
அரம்பா வுன்னை யறிந்துகொண் டேனுனக் கஞ்சுவ னம்மம் தரவே
en: Lord who, when all the calves and cows gathered to eat
the unripe ears of red rice in the paddy field, tall [like] sugar-cane
grabbed and threw a single unwelcome calf
in order to fell a wood-apple fruit!
Trickster who placed a net to surround a virgin girl
with soft curls full of bees [and] transformed [her]!
I have come to know you
[and] I am afraid to give you [my] breast milk
Splendour who, entering the grove of that herder village
with [your] soft flute full of enticement [and,]
placing [it] to [your] lips, stood while maidens with soft curls
and coiled garlands came, surrounded and worshipped you!
Now I have no other fortune, my lord
but the misfortune of getting you
Rascal! I have come to know you
[and] I am afraid to give you [my] breast

ta: வாளா வாகிலும் காணகில் லார்பிறர் மக்களை மையன்மை செய்து
தோளா லிட்டவ ரோடு திளைத்துநீ சொல்லப் படாதன செய்தாய்
கேளா ரயர் குலத்தவ ரிப்பழி கெட்டேன்வாழ் வில்லை நந்தற்
காளா யுன்னை யறிந்துகொண் டேனுனக்கஞ்சுவ னம்மம் தரவே
en: Even if [your wickedness] comes to nought
having infatuated the ladies [of the village]
the others will not see [it this way]
Having embraced them, grasping [their] shoulders
you have done unspeakable things
Those of the herder clan will not tolerate these crimes!
I am ruined! I have no life!
Ruler of Nanda! I have come to know you
[and] I am afraid to give you [my] breast milk

ta: தாய்மார் மோர்விற்கப் போவர் தமப்பன்மார் கற்றா நிறைப்பின் புபோவர்
நீயாய்ப் பாடி யிளங்கன்னி மார்களை நேர்பட வேகொண்டு போதி
காய்வார்க் கென்று முகப்பன வேசெய்து கண்டார் கழறத் திரியும்
ஆயா வுன்னை யறிந்துகொண் டேனுனக் கஞ்சுவ னம்மம் தரவே
en: [Their] mothers go to sell buttermilk
[Their] fathers go to follow the herd of cows and [their] calves
You go to abduct the young virgins of the herder village!
Always giving satisfaction to those who are furious, you, herder boy
wander about so that they see you and grumble
I have come to know you
[and] I am afraid to give you [my] breast milk
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person, dative
pronominalised noun, third person, neuter plural
participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

ta: தொத்தார் பூங்குழல் கன்னி யொருத்தியைச் சோலைத் தடம்கொண்டு புக்கு
முத்தார் கொங்கை புணர்ந்திரா நாழிகை மூவேழு சென்றபின் வந்தாய்
ஒத்தார்க் கொத்தன பேசுவ ருன்னை யுரப்பவே நானொன்றும் மாட்டேன்
அத்தா வுன்னை யறிந்துகொண் டேனுனக் கஞ்சுவ னம்மம் தரவே
en: Taking one maiden, her curls full of blossom clusters
into the huge grove
and embracing her pearl laden breasts [all] night
you returned only after 21 nāḻikais
They will say what is appropriate for those who are appropriate
[but] I am not able to frighten you at all, Lord!
I have come to know you
[and] I am afraid to give you [my] breast milk
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, third person, dative
perfective aspect, participial noun, neuter plural

ta: கரார் மேனி நிறத்தெம் பிரானைக் கடிகமழ் பூங்குழ லாய்ச்சி
ஆரா வின்னமு துண்ணத் தருவன்நா னம்மம்தா ரேனென்ற மாற்றம்
பாரார் தொல்புக ழான்புது வைமன்னன் பட்டர் பிரான்சொன்ன பாடல்
ஏரா ரின்னிசை மாலைவல் லாரி ருடீகே சனடி யாரே
en: Those who master this garland of sweet music full of beauty
[these] verses composed by Lord Scholar, King of Putuvai
he whose ancient fame fills the world
on the words of the herdess with curling hair [full of] fragrant flowers
To our lord with the black-hued body, saying
“I will give [you] unlimited sweet nectar to eat
[but] I will not give [you my] breast”
Are servants of Hṛṣīkeśa
After performing ablutions
for the tender sprout of the herder lineage, the kohl-hued one
why did I send [my] child after the calves
to stop him from wandering in each of the houses?
[Now] the ankleted feet that tormented Kaṃsa ache
Ah! What a sin!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person, accusative
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person, accusative

en: To stop him from wandering everywhere
getting up to mischief in the village
Destroying the sand houses along with the girls
besmeared with lasting turmeric [paste]
Why did I send my child after the calves into the midst of the forest
with hunters and dust from the claves?
Ah! What a sin!
To stop him with the gold and sapphire [hued] body
from wandering about playing in dust
With girls [adorned] with beautiful jeweled girdles everyday
I sent my sapphire-hued one after the calves on the forest path
that thunders like bells on a mountain
Alas! What a sin!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: To stop him from wandering everywhere in this village
doing many things
So that ladies with beautiful black curls come to spread gossip
after the claves on the forest path
Ah! What a sin!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: To stop him from entering this and that place
as one who is intimate with the women of those shepherds
giving [them his] kovvai fruit lips and caressing [them]
I sent the leader of the gods after the calves in the forest
with hunters who have bows that cause pain
Ah! What a sin!

ta: மிடறு மெழுமெழுத் தோட வெண்ணெய் விழுங்கிப் போய்
en: To stop him from wandering everywhere in this village
going around, devouring butter so that it runs softly [down his] neck
committing many misdeeds
I sent my child stubling after the calves on the forest path
where many elephants wander
Ah! What a sin!
To stop him from wandering about frolicking and playing with [his] friends
So that ladies with creeper thin waists come spreading gossip
I sent the leader [who rides a] bird after the calves
on the hot forest path with dried spurge
Alas! What a sin!
Just as he was kept in the womb for 12 months
I have raised [him] and fed [him] the nectar of my young breasts
I sent my young lion after the calves in the forest at dawn
so that [now his] golden feet ache
Alas! What a sin!
I didn’t give a parasol and leather sandals to Dāmodara
[yet] this cruel woman, sent my child after the calves
in the harsh, hot forest
with broken, sharp, painful, hot stones
so that [now his] leg and feet ache
Ah! What a sin!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, neuter plural

en: For those who can master [this] garland of sweet Tamil
the words of the scholar king of those of Putuvai
with mansions that glitter with gold
“I sent my jewel hued one, him who is always sweet to me, after the calves,”
that were spoken by Yaśodā
there is no suffering
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

ta: சீலைக் குதம்பை யொருகா தொருகாது செந்நிற மேல்தோன் றிப்பூ
கோலப் பணைக்கச்சும் கூறை யுடையும் குளிர்முத்தின் கோடா லமும்
காலிப்பின் னேவருகின் றகடல்வண் ணன்வேடத் தைவந்து காணீர்
ஞாலத்துப் புத்திரனைப் பெற்றார்நங் கைமீர்நா னேமற்றா ருமில்லை
en: Ladies who begot a son upon the earth!
Look at [his] garb, the sea-hued one, following after the cow herd
a cloth earlobe stretcher in one ear
and a red lily blossom in the other
a garment with a thick, beautiful sash
and a crooked necklace of cooling pearls
There is no better [than] mine
gloss: participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

ta: கன்னிநன் மாமதிள் சூழ்தரு பூம்பொழில் காவிரித் தென்ன ரங்கம்
மன்னிய சீர்மது சூதனா கேசவா பாவியேன் வாழ்வு கந்து
உன்னை யிளங்கன்று மேய்க்கச் சிறுகாலே யூட்டி யொருப்ப டுத்தேன்
என்னின் மனம்வலி யாளொரு பெணில்லை யென்குட்ட னேமுத் தம்தா
en: Madhusūdana of enduring excellence
in Southern Araṅkam on [the banks of]
The Kāveri with flower groves surrounded by fresh
beautiful, big natural walls! Kesavā!
Sinful me, desiring a happy life, I agreed to feed you at dawn
so that [you could] graze the young calves
There is no other woman as hard of heart than me
My boy! Give [me] a kiss!

ta: காடுக ளூடுபோய்க் கன்றுகள் மேய்த்து மறியோடி கார்க்கோ டல்பூச்
சூடி வருகின்ற தாமோ தராகற்றுத் தூளிகா ணுன்னு டம்பு
பேடை மயிற்சாயல் பின்னை மணாளா நீராட்ட மைத்து வைத்தேன்
ஆடி யமுதுசெ யப்பனு முண்டில னுன்னோ டுடனே யுண்பான்
en: Dāmodara who comes adorned with dark lily blossoms
Having gone to the forest, grazing and herding the claves!
Look [at you]! Your body [covered] in dust from the calves
Bridegroom of Piṉṉai with the likeness of a pea-hen!
I have prepared [your] bath. [Come] take [your] bath and eat!
[Your] father has not eaten [yet]; he will eat with you

ta: கடியார் பொழிலணி வேங்கட வாகரும் போரேறே நீயு கக்கும்
குடையும் செருப்பும் குழலும் தருவிக்கக் கொள்ளாதே போனாய் மாலே
கடிய வெங்கா னிடைக்கன்றின் பின்போ னசிறுக் குட்டச்செங் கமல
அடியும் வெதும்பியுன் கண்கள் சிவந்தா யசைந்திட்டாய் நீயெம் பிரான்
en: Lord of beautiful Vēṅkaṭa with fragrant groves!
Black battle bull!
Māl! You left without bringing along [your] parasol
leather sandals, and flute, which you need
Little boy who went after the calves into the cruel, hot forest
[your] red lotus feet are hot and your eyes are red
My Lord, you are completely exhausted!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, vocative, third person

ta: பற்றார் நடுங்கமுன் பாஞ்சசன் னியத்தை வாய்வைத்த போரேறே யென்
சிற்றாயர் சிங்கமே சீதை மணாளா சிறுக்குட்டச் செங்கண் மாலே
சிற்றாடை யும்சிறுப் பத்திர முமிவை கட்டிலின் மேல்வைத் துப்போய்
கற்றாய ரோடுநீ கன்றுகள் மேய்த்துக் கலந்துடன் வந்தாய் போலும்
en: Battle bull who placed [your] lips to Pāñcajanya long ago
so that [your] enemies trembled!
My little lion of the herders! Bridegroom of Sītā!
Little Boy! Red eyed Māl!
Having placed [your] little garment and toy dagger on [your] cot and left
It seems you went off with the calf-herders to graze the calves

ta: அஞ்சுட ராழியுன் கையகத் தேந்தும் அழகாநீ பொய்கை புக்கு
நஞ்சுமிழ் நாகத்தி னோடு பிணங்கவும் நானுயிர் வாழ்ந்தி ருந்தேன்
என்செய்ய வென்னை வயிறு மறுக்கினா யேதுமோ ரச்ச மில்லை
கஞ்சன் மனத்துக் குகப்பன வேசெய்தாய் காயாம்பூ வண்ணம் கொண்டாய்
en: Beauty who holds the fine fiery discus in the palm [of your hands]!
I went on living [my] life
even though you fought the venom spitting snake in that pond
What [am I] to do? You make my stomach hurt!
You fear nothing at all
The things you did were a pleasure to the mind of Kaṃsa
Oh you who took the colour of the Kāyā flower!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, neuter plural
participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect

ta: பன்றியு மாமையும் மீனமு மாகிய பாற்கடல் வண்ணா வுன்மேல்
கன்றி னுருவாகி மேய்புலத் தேவந்த கள்ள வசுரன் தன்னை
சென்று பிடித்துச் சிறுக்கைக ளாலே விளங்கா யெறிந்தாய் போலும்
என்றுமென் பிள்ளைக்குத் தீமைகள் செய்வார்க ளங்ஙன மாவார் களே
en: You with the complexion of the milk ocean
who became the boar, the tortoise, and the fish!
With [your] little hands, approaching and seizing
that demon who came in the field to graze
in the form of a calf [to] deceive you
[now] it seems you have thrown an unripe fruit of the wood-apple tree
those who harass my child always end up like that!

ta: கேட்டறி யாதன கேட்கின்றேன் கேசவா கோவல ரிந்தி ரற்கு
காட்டிய சோறுங் கறியுந் தயிருங் கலந்துட னுண்டாய் போலு
மூட்ட முதலிலே னுன்தன்னைக் கொண்டொரு போதுமெனக் கரிது
வாட்ட மிலாப்புகழ் வாசுதே வாவுன்னை யஞ்சுவ னின்று தொட்டும்
en: Kesava, I am hearing unfathomable things!
It seems that, having mixed up the rice, curry, and curd
that the herders offered to Indra
You ate [them all up] at once!
I do not have the money to feed [you]
it is difficult for me [to] provide for you at this time
Vāsudeva of unfading glory! Now I am beginning to fear you

ta: திண்ணார்வெண் சங்குடை யாய்திரு நாள்திரு வோணமின் றேழு நாள் முன்
பண்ணேர் மொழியாரைக் கூவி முளையட்டிப் பல்லாண்டு கூறு வித்தேன்
கண்ணாலம் செய்யக் கறியும் கலத்த தரிசியு மாக்கி வைத்தேன்
en: Bearer of the powerful white conch
7 days from now is the holy day of Ōṇam
Having summoned those with melodious speech and planted the sprouts
I caused “many years’ to be intoned
I made curry and rice for the festival and put [them] in pots
Kaṇṇaṉ! From tomorrow on, do not go after the calves
Stay here and make [yourself] beautiful
gloss: participial noun, singular, vocative, second person
causative, perfective aspect, first person, singular

ta: புற்றர வல்கு லசோதைநல் லாய்ச்சி தன் புத்திரன் கோவிந் தனை
கற்றினம் மேய்த்து வரக்கண் டுகந்தவள் கற்பித்த மாற்ற மெல்லாம்
செற்றமி லாதவர் வாழ்தரு தென்புது வைவிட் டுசித் தன்சொல்
கற்றிவை பாடவல் லார்கடல் வண்ணன் கழலிணை காண்பார் களே
en: Those who are able to sing these calf[-songs] composed by Viṭṭucittaṉ of Putuvai in the South
where those without enmity live happily
[on] all the words of command of the good herdess Yaśodā
with hips [like] a serpent in an ant-hill
[spoken] when, seeing her son Govinda return
having grazed the calf herd, she rejoiced
They will see the Sea-hued Lord’s pair of feet
Seeing the friends that come [along with] Govinda
waving peacock fans and peacock feathers
with big drums, single-headed drums, flutes
with dangling peacock feathers, and songs everywhere
Maidens, grasping the opening of [their] latticed windows
exclaim,“That’s not the rain cloud coming is it?”
[and] while they creep [through their windows] and stand [in awe]
they place [him] in the entirety of [their] hearts
and forget to eat!
gloss: present tense, third person, neuter singular

en: Don’t stand there obstructing the boy
when he comes during the evening
in the midst of a group of many herders adorned by jasmine blossoms
with good fragrance and Kino tree blossoms
in the middle of many peacock feathers on [his] big waist sash
wearing a dagger as thin as a lizard
with garments like the slender leaves of a creeper
spreading over, adorning his faultless holy hips
[and] lose your bunch of bangles
As [his] friends run with [his] knife, small bow, bat, and shawl
With one hand resting on the shoulder of another [boy]
[and with the other holding] the conch
that he blows to call back the cow herd
she sees the turmeric colour, body, and beauty of [my] boy Kaṇṇaṉ
who weakens upon return
My girl stood right next to [him] and stared
Seeing that, something will surely be said in this village
gloss: present tense, third person, neuter singular

en: Girls! Come and see the lord who protected the cow herd
by raising a mountian as a herder
Seeing him coming in the street playing [his] flute
along with his friends after grazing the claves
Ladies, I know I have never seen anyone like him
[My] bangles slip off, not even one staying put
[and] even [my] sari[-clad] ample young breasts are not in my control
gloss: participial noun, accusative, third person, imperfective aspect
participial noun, singular, first person, negative

en: I watched as he sang and danced
getting and staying in front of the herders
adorned by the eye of a peacock feather in [his] curly hair
while herders stood around [him] with fans of peacock feathers
Hereafter, I cannot tolerate talk of me [being]
for any other except for our Māyaṉ of Māliruñcōlai
Considering that she belongs to the Victor, give [her to him]!
If [you] do not give [her], there will be trouble!
gloss: proper name, singular, masculine, dative, third person

en: Knowing this and that about the limitless herder boy
if he passes through this street
with a properly applied tilaka on his holy forehead
so that it shines, holy curls, and a holy forehead ornament
coming along with the herders under the forest of cool leaves
[playing] a heavenly drum
while [he] swings his crooked stick [around]
[we will] surround and detain [him] saying “he took [our] ball,”
[and in this way,] friend, we will see the smile upon [his] coral[-red] lips
Behind the massive herd, beneath a forest of foliage
as his holy body continues to shine brightly
[his] tuft of hair pleasantly fragrant with blue lotuses
[and] adorned with peacock feathers
in the midst of a group of many herders
playing [his] flute, singing songs
[and] dancing along with the herder [boys]
as [he] rolls [his] beautiful red lotus eyes
my daughter saw the beauty of the cowherd boy
who came [along] noisily [and] forgets [herself]
gloss: causative, present tense, third person, neuter singular

en: Standing there face-to-face with the cowherd boy
who comes like Indra
having taken saffron powder [and] applied [it] to [his] head
[he] placed the tiru nāmam there by means of a single leaf
[and] adorned his curly hair
with beautiful peacock feathers without [any] gaps
while I say ‘Don’t lose [your] collection of bangles!’
Ladies! You saw [her] standing at the crossroads
her bangles, along with her sari become loose and slip off!
gloss: present tense, third person, neuter singular

en: [When] my girl saw the beauty of the herder boy who came with a flourish—
adorned with forest jasmine garlands and wild jasmine garlands
having placed a malabar lily blossom on [his] right ear
with [his] curly hair hanging low as decoration
holding [his] sweet flute to [his] lips, playing and playing—
desire arising [in her]
you saw [her] blocking [him], not remaining still
standing face-to-face [with him]
[Her] white bangles have become loose [and her] body becomes thin
gloss: present tense, third person, neuter singular

en: Those who are devotees who joyfully sing in melodies
[this] garland of ten [verses] composed by Viṭṭucittaṉ
king of those of Putuvai with groves where bees dwell
about the way that the young maidens experienced desire
[upon] seeing Kaṇṇaṉ appear behind the herd of cows
in the middle of the street in the herder village
in order to grace [them]
[while] the celestials in the highest heavens toil
to worship [him] intensely
they will reach highest Vaikunta!
The mountain that was borne by the one with a complexion [like] the great, churning sea
who brought about the enmity of the rain clouds
after [he] swiftly and thoroughly ate
the heaping mountain of cooked rice
river of curd, and bog of ghee
called Govardhana
where little girls catch simple, round
wide eyed fawn in nets and take [them]
to give [them] milk on the end of a cloth knot
[to suckle] and raise [them]
is [his] victory umbrella
The mountain that was raised and upended by Madhusudana
who blocked the rains from coming and pouring for 7 days
when the king of the celestials of faultless deed
angrily sent [them] by way of [his] power
called Govardana
where the nervous [elephant], hastily grasping
[her] newborn calf, placing the infant between [her] legs
[and] turned to fight the young lion [that was] stalking [it]
is [his] victory umbrella
gloss: negative, verbal noun, third person, neuter singular

en: The mountain that our father lifted, with the shining discus in hand
when, weeping, the simple herdesses
with wide, beautiful, kohl [lined] eyes
cow-herders, and herds of cows begged
“please accept our request for refuge,”
called Govardana
where big shouldered mountain men bend their bows
saying,“look [at] the deer herd grazing in the uplands,”
to ladies who [then] say to them, “[give] them refuge”
is [his] victory umbrella!
The mountain where the Lord of celestials stood
having placed [his] hand
in order to grasp the base [and] pluck [it] up
as if he picked up and tossed a ball of rice
to a gaping mouthed, red-eyed elephant
called Govardana
where—the clouds moving to the sea, dipping down
sinking in, and drawing up the water everywhere
so that it is diminished [from the sea] —
the rain flows as if from a water pot
is [his] victory umbrella!
The mountain that our father, supreme lord
having taken the form of a boar
took and raised up [as if it was] a clod of dirt
as if saying “Heavenly residents!
Why don’t you come and take [it] if you’re stong enough?”
called Govardana
where stood the rutting forest elepant
having lost its tusk, raised its trunk
as it oozed the descending ichor
[and] looked up longingly at the curbed crescent moon
is [his] victory umbrella!
gloss: participial noun, plural, second person, vocative

en: The mountain that Tirumāl, possessed of righteousness
[used to] cover [the cowherds]
holding [it] with all five fingers of his red lotus hand
as the spokes
[and his] long sapphire [hued] arm as the shaft
called Govardana
where clear waterfalls descend, spreading everywhere
appear as if as a coat of shining strings of jewels
and glittering pearls
is [his] victory umbrella!
The huge mountain that Dāmodara bore
[by] spreading the five fingers of [his] broad hand
Like the king of the serpents, [his] many hoods spread
who bore the vast earth in repose
Called Govardhana
Where female monkeys, taking their young
in the palm of [their] hands, put [them] to sleep
Singing the glory of Hanuman who
having gone to Laṅkā, utterly annihilated [its] might
Is [his] victory umbrella
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular

en: The mountain that Nārāyaṇa [used to] protect the vanguard
as if graspping a shield
when a multitude of massive rain clouds [came]
pouring down arrow[-like] rain all over the battle field
[as] the war raged, creating havoc
called Govardhana
where angry tigers with murderous mouths
having gone inside huts of leaves and bamboo
as sages great with tapas sit scratching their necks
while they remain sleeping
is [his] victory umbrella!
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular
imperfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular
participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

en: The great mountain that
having been given His name
was borne upon the earth by Damodara
—he with the mouth that ate [from] the breast of the mighty demoness—
standing like a strong pillar bearing a heavy burden
called Govardhana
where monkey troops teach their young
having been placed on [their] backs
to leap and reach for branches while showing the way forward
is [his] victory umbrella!
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: The mountain of the jewel coloured one
The beauty of the fingers of [his] red lotus hands
spreading [like] a creeper did not fail or faulter
[and] the divine finger nails, [their] beauty growing
were not damaged, [what] a wonder!
called Govardhana
where rain pours down everywhere, settling in
as many clusters of black clouds ascend the summit
[appearing] as if the front side [of the mountain] has faded
is [his] victory umbrella!
gloss: negative, perfective aspect, third person, neuter plural
negative, perfective aspect, third person, neuter plural
perfective aspect, third person, neuter plural

en: Devotees who have goodness in [their] minds
that praise [this] garland of ten [verses]
composed by the lord [and] shining scholar of Puttūr
[where] Brahmins flourish in holiness
on the victory umbrella called Govardhana
where jasmine creepers stay, slumbering on bottle flowers
of him who rides the enemy of snakes
[who] has a serpent bed, [who] drove off the serpent
[they] will reach supreme Vaikuntha!
Ladies living in the great country of Nāvalam!
Listen to this miracle
The way the flute sounds upon the pure lips of Tirumāl
with the pure right-whorled conch!
Everywhere, the cowherd girls’ bodies and minds fade
as [their] young breasts rejoice
Escaping their guardians, they come as a threaded garland
shyly bowing their heads
When Govinda played [his] flute with the corner of [his] mouth
such that [his cheek] appeared [like] a round belly
the left side of [his] jaw bent to [his] left shoulder
[his] two hands united [with his flute]
and [his] eyebrows arched up
the maidens
like female deer and simple peacocks
as [their] blossomed tresses become loose
[and] garments slip off
grasping at [their] saris with one hand, trembling
stood [still] while [their] line streaked eyes ran [after him]
When Govinda
the prince of heaven, the darling of Vaikuntha
Vāsudeva, king of Mathūrā
Prince of king Nanda, darling of the herders
Played [his] flute
Heavenly young ladies came and gathered
[their] hearts melting
[their] flower[-like] eyeswelling with tears
[their] thick, fragrant tresses becoming loose
[and] stood, ears afixed [to the sound], as [their] foreheads perspired
When the dark lad played [his] flute
while walking about in the forest
crushing and trampling the scorched weeds
called Dhenuka, Pralamba, and Kāliya
on earth and in heaven
Menakā, Tilottamā, Urvaśī, Rambhā and [the other] Apsaras
shy and bewildered
without [even] opening [their] mouths
ceased singing and dancing
When the music of the flute at the mouth of Madhusūdana
who terrified the kings of the three worlds
when, as a man-lion long ago
[he] destroyed the superiority of the Asura
grasped and carried away the ears of Tumburu and Nārada
with good stringed instruments
they disregarded their vīṇās, and the Kiṉṉara couples declared
“We cannot touch our lutes!”
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Listen to the distressing experiences
of those who heard when our Supreme lord
He with the big, broad, red eyes
He with the bulging arms
Devakī’s boy, Lion of the Gods
played [his] flute today!
All the Gāndharvas who wander the heavens were caught
by the net of [his] nectar[-like] song
saying, “Our burden is no more”
becoming shy and bewildered
languishing and dispirited
they stood, restraining their hands
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, third person, plural
perfective aspect, participial noun, third person, neuter plural

en: Listen to the miracle I saw upon the earth!
When he on the serpent bed played [his] flute
among the assembly of the young herder clan
that was grazing cattle
so that the sound arose to the celestial world
[such that] all the celestials, forgetting [their] food offerings
hastened to crowd into the herder village
taking in and delighting in the sweet taste [of his song]
with the tongue in [their] ears
following Govinda everywhere
they were unable to depart [from him]
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, noun, singular, relative
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: When Govinda played [his] flute
[his] little fingers pressing down to play
[his] red eyes curving
[his] red lips pursed
[his] brow overhung with beads of sweat
Groups of birds leaving [their] nests, come circling
descending to settle in the big forest
[and] herds of milk cows stretch [their] legs
bow [their] heads, and settle down
[such that] even [their] ears do not twitch
The way the sound of the flute that was played
by the one with the face where dark, curly hair hangs
Like a group of bees that surrounds a red lotus flower
him with the hue of round, abundant, high rain clouds
[made] the bewildered herd of deer forget [their] grazing
so that the grazed grass fell from the corners of their mouths
[and], without swaying to either side, nor shifting in place
They stood like embellishments on a painting
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: When the herder with the form of a precious jewel
the lord, the unique one
with golden clothes donned well
tying on and wearing peacock feathers with dark eyes
played [his] flute
the trees, remaining [in place]
seeing Tirumāl, standing on all sides
released [their] blossoms that spread [their] star[-shaped] pollen
[and] bent low [their] long branches
[as if] weeping and closing [the eyes]
[Such] is the merit they have done
Those who master the Tamil [verses] expounded by Viṭṭucittaṉ
king of Putuvai, where flutes and drums resound
About the flood of nectar that bubbles and rises to the suface
from the holes of the flute on the beautiful lips of Govinda
with a hairknot where [his] black curly tresses abound
[their] voices becoming pleasant like [his] flute
they will be held in high regard in the assembly of the good folk
Lord! Her body covered in dust, [her] speech vexed
She is not able to cover [her] hips
with the the small garment [made] of red thread!
She cannot even part from the winnow and
little toy utensils in [her] hands!
[Yet here] she comes [her] hand-in-hand
with him who sleeps on the hooded serpent bed!
[Her] teeth do not rise above [her] lips!
[Her] hair hasn’t gathered into a knot!
Having befriended a few girls with little heads
that do not bow [with modesty]
consenting to ruinous liasons
she wanders back speaking as honourably as usual
She is suffering from a delusion about the great jewel toned Māyaṉ
If [before she] was making toy houses
with piles of white sand in the courtyard
[now she] is making nothing but [His] conch
discus, staff, sword, and bow!
[Her] breast [have] not [even] grown round yet
Being fearful about her with Govinda
my heart is becoming [more] disturbed each day
Many friends came, disparaging my daughter
a foolish, simple child
to whom do I speak
about [their] intention to lead [her] astray?
Having pushed [her] into the deep pool
called “discus-bearer”
you have trapped [her]
She does not [know] the old saying
“a ladle does not taste the salt”
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Adorned with garlands of fine tulasī
going recognized in coutryside and city
She searches, wandering everywhere that Nāraṇaṉ went
There are many residents who would ruin [us]
being troubled, [they] say over and over
“Watch her with Keśava, keep her near!”
gloss: present tense, participial noun, third person
perfective aspect, third person, noun, singular

en: For me, who raised [her] providing [all her] wants
affixing [her] forehead ornament
[and] adorning [her] with golden earrings
an anklet and ankle bells
she has no [desire] to be with me
Suddenly running, going and staying outside
saying “Pūvai flower[-hued] Lord”
Ladies with ringlettes in your hair! She has gone mad!
gloss: participial noun, singular, dative, first person, perfective aspect

en: She is the foolish, simple girl of me, a simple woman
who, even if I [want to] speak, I cannot
Like a ladle that has slipped from [its] handle
she sounds like a parrot
saying “Keśava” and “Imperishable One”
in front of those who remain without shame
Ladies with long, fragrant tresses! She has gone mad!
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, negative, second person, singular, vocative

en: She, who wears a golden necklace
looks in the mirror, shakes the bangles on her hand
puts on [her] garments, becomes weak
arranging her kovvai red lips
standing, gaining strength, babbles
about the goodness of god [and his] thousand names
has gone mad for the changeless, dark jewel hued [lord]!

ta: கைத்தலத் துள்ளமா டழியக் கண் ணாலங்கள் செய்திவளை
en: What is the use in keeping her [here]
conducting marriages so that the wealth [we have] on hand is spent?
[It will only] bring reproach to us
Like a seedling reared for transplanting that grows in a field
Leave [her] to grow up with the huge, dark cloud hued [lord]
[he can] do whatever he [wants with her]
While we were preparing to perform a huge marriage ceremony
thinking to keep her in our home, she thought something [else]
Before [anyone] says that she turned away the treatment
bring them together, [place] her at the side
of he who measured the earth!
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: For those who master the garland of ten [verses] composed by Viṭṭucittaṉ
king of the people of Putuvai, surrounded by beautiful groves
about the words spoken by a mother
saying, “Having gone mad for Nārāyaṇa who
having consumed the entire earth
sleeps on a banyan leaf, she rejoices”
there will be no suffering

ta: நல்லதோர் தாமரைப் பொய்கை நாண்மலர் மேல்பனி சோர
அல்லியுந் தாதுமு திர்ந்திட் டழகழிந் தாலொத் ததாலோ
இல்லம் வெறியோடிற் றாலோ வென்மக ளையெங்குங் காணேன்
மல்லரை யட்டவன் பின்போய் மதுரைப் புறம்புக்காள் கொலோ
en: When dew drops on the day’s blossom in the lovely lotus pond
[causing its] petals and pollen to fall away
is it not the case that [its] beauty is ruined?
[This] house has become mad, has it not?
I don’t see my daughter anywhere!
Has she gone after the one who killed the wrestlers
[and] entered the city of Mathurā?
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, noun, singular
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular

ta: ஒன்று மறிவொன்றில் லாத வுருவறைக் கோபாலர் தங்கள்
கன்றுகால் மாறுமா போலே கன்னியிருந் தாளைக் கொண்டு
நன்றும் கிறிசெய்து போனான் நாராயணன் செய்த தீமை
என்று மெமர்கள் குடிக்கோ ரேச்சுக் கொலாயிடுங் கொலோ
en: The mischief perpetrated by Nārāyaṇaṉ who
like an unattractive herder
without knowledge of anything at all
comes along with clever trickery [and] takes her, [our] virgin girl
as if stealing a calf
has become a constant affliction of abuse to our clan, has it not?
gloss: participial noun, singular, feminine, accusative, third person
singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect, participial noun

ta: குமரிம ணஞ்செய்து கொண்டு கோலஞ்செய் தில்லத் திருத்தி
தமரும் பிறருமறி யத்தா மோதரற் கென்று சாற்றி
யமரர் பதியுடைத் தேவி யரசா ணியைவழி பட்டு
துமில மெழப்பறை கொட்டித் தோரணம் நாட்டிடுங் கொலோ
en: They will perform a marriage [for the] girl
adorning [her] with [the appropriate] garments
seating her in the hall, [and] announcing that [she is]
for Dāmodara so that relations and others know
the wife of the immortals’ lord
adhering to the [ritual of the] pipal branch
beating drums so that the din rises
[and] set up a festooned archway, won’t they?

ta: ஒருமகள் தன்னை யுடையே னுலகம் நிறைந்த புகழால்
திருமகள் போல வளர்த்தேன் செங்கண்மால் தான்கொண்டு போனான்
பெருமக ளாய்க்குடி வாழ்ந்து பெரும்பிள்ளை பெற்றவ சோதை
மருமக ளைக்கண்டு கந்து மணாட்டுப் புறஞ்செய்யுங் கொலோ
en: I have one daughter. I raised [her] like the lady Tiru [herself]
with praise that filled the world
Red-eyed Māl took her and left
Yaśodā who, being the great lady living with the clan
begot that great boy
joyfully seeing [her] daughter-in-law
will cherish [this] bride
won’t she?
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect

ta: தம்மாமன் நந்தகோ பாலன் தழீஇக் கொண் டென்மகள் தன்னை
செம்மாந்தி ரேயென்று சொல்லிச் செழுங்கயற் கண்ணுஞ்செவ் வாயும்
கொம்மை முலையு மிடையும் கொழும்பணைத் தோள்களுங் கண்டிட்டு
இம்மக ளைப்பெற்ற தாய ரினித்தரி யாரென்னுங் கொலோ
en: Nanda Gopāla, her uncle, embracing [her]
saying “You are appropriate”
seeing [her] beautiful kayal eyes, red lips
round breasts, waist, and plump bamboo arms
will think
“how can the mother who begot this girl carry on now?”
won’t he?

ta: வேடர் மறக்குலம் போலே வேண்டிற்றுச் செய்தென் மகளை
கூடிய கூட்டமே யாகக் கொண்டு குடிவாழுங் கொலோ
நாடும் நகரும றிய நல்லதோர் கண்ணாலஞ் செய்து
சாடிறப் பாய்ந்த பெருமான் தக்கவா கைப்பற்றுங் கொலோ
en: Will [he] take my daughter in a consentual union
[and] live together, doing whatever he wants [with her]
like the angry clan of hunters?
Or will the lord who lept in order to break the cart
get her hand in an appropriate manner [and]
perform a proper marriage so that it is known
to countryside and city [alike]?
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

ta: அண்டத் தமரர் பெருமா னாழியா னின்றென் மகளை
பண்டப் பழிப்புக்கள் சொல்லிப் பரிசற வாண்டிடுங் கொலோ
கொண்டு குடிவாழ்க்கை வாழ்ந்து கோவலப் பட்டங் கவித்து
பண்டை மணாட்டிமார் முன்னே பாதுகா வல்வைக்குங் கொலோ
en: Now, will the Lord of the heavenly immortals, the discus-bearer
disparage my daughter’s belongings
[and] receive her without honour?
Or will [he], having accepted [her], live a prosperous family life
crowning [her] queen of the cowherds
[and] provide protection [for her]
in front of [his] previous brides?
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

ta: குடியில் பிறந்தவர் செய்யுங் குணமொன் றுஞ்செய்தி லனந்தோ
நடையொன்றுஞ் செய்திலன் நங்காய் நந்தகோ பன்மகன் கண்ண
னிடையிரு பாலும் வணங்க விளைத்திளைத் தென்மக ளெங்கி
கடைகயி றேபற்றி வாங்கிக் கைதழும் பேறிடுங் கொலோ
en: Alas! He has not done one thing of quality
which are done by those born to [his] clan
Ladies! Kaṇṇaṉ, Nandagōpa’s son
has not done one thing [according to] custom
Will my daughter, languishing, grow weaker and weaker
so that both sides of her waist bend
Becoming exhausted, grasping the churning rope
welts rising on her hands
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, third person

ta: வெண்ணிறத் தோய்தயிர் தன்னை வெள்வரைப் பின்முனெ ழுந்து
கண்ணுறங் காதே யிருந்து கடையவுந் தான்வல்லள் கொலோ
வொண்ணிறத் தாமரைச் செங்க ணுலகளந் தானென் மகளை
பண்ணறை யாப்பணி கொண்டு பரிசற வாண்டிடுங் கொலோ
en: Will she, rising before dawn
[her] eyes being without sleep
be able to churn the curds
so that they curdle into a white colour?
Will he who measured the world
[his] red eyes [like] the bright coloured lotus
take [her] in service in a manner that is without dharma
[and] rule her without dignity?
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, third person

ta: மாயவன் பின்வழி சென்று வழியிடை மாற்றங்கள் கேட்
டாயர்கள் சேரியி லும்புக் கங்குத்தை மாற்றமு மெல்லாந்
தாயவள் சொல்லிய சொல்லைத் தண்புது வைப்பட்டன் சொன்ன
தூயத மிழ்ப்பத்தும் வல்லார் தூமணி வண்ணனுக்கா ளரே
en: Those who master [this] ten of pure Tamil
composed by the scholar of cool Putuvai
about the words that were spoken by [this] mother
going along the path following Māyavaṉ
asking questions on the path
[and,] having entered the herder village
all the words [she spoke] in that place
they are devotees of the pure jewel hued [lord]
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, dative, third person

en: Jump and sing about the strength of my lord who
spontaneously plucked the tree of fresh flowers
with [the help of his] strong, loud bird
while the lord of her who would not give the flower of love
to the goddess of my lord looked on that day
Jump and sing about the strength of our master!
Jump and sing about the strength of the bow of him who
having taken and bent the virtue along with the bow of him
who came as a rival saying
“Go look at the strength of my bow”
before seizing the bow
consumed the life of the old woman
Jump and sing about the nature of Dāśarathi!
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: Jump and sing about the strength of him who
with desire rising, lifted and carried away
the lady Rukmiṇī in [his] chariot
[and] shaved the head of the prideful one
having swiftly come there in opposition
so that [his] bravery was broken
Jump and sing about the lion of Devakī!
gloss: singular, masculine, perfective aspect, participial noun
participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine, singular

en: Jump and sing about him who is without anger, who
when [his] step-mother approached
[him and] said “go to the forest!
[and] his own mother followed after
[him] weeping, “our Lord!”
went to the cruel forest
when the mother of death commanded [it]
Jump and sing about the bridegroom of Sītā!
gloss: negative, participial noun, masculine, singular, accusative

en: Jump and sing about the kohl coloured one who
as a messenger to the Five, assited in the Bhārata war
[and,] having entered the good pond
where dwelt a snake spitting poison
showed grace, leaping on [its] hood so that it was afraid
Jump and sing about the lion of Yaśodā!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Jump and sing about the one who gave [his] sandals
to prince Bharata
with incomparable qualities
who followed behind [Him] that day saying
“Accept the crown, rule the three worlds
grace me - your servant!”
Jump and sing about the king of Ayodhyā!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, dative, first person
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, accusative

en: Jump and sing about the heroism of the strong-armed Sage who
leaping in to disturb the pond of Kāḷiya
standing on [his] five tall heads and dancing
Graced him so that [he was] liberated
Jump and sing about the pure jewel hued one!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Jump and sing about he who
having given [his] kingdom and [his royal] garland
to [his] younger brother
[and] gone to the Daṇḍaka forest
at the word of the scheming woman
cut off the nose along with the ears of Śūrpaṇakhā
with a thin waist
so that [she] howled!
Jump and sing about the king of Ayodhyā!
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, feminine, singular
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, accusative

en: Jump and sing about the bull of the cowherders who
kicked the deceptive cart, smashed the marutu trees
went with the herders, [and] protected the cow herd
stood as a sage, playing [his] jeweled bamboo flute!
Jump and sing about he who grazed the cow herd!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, accusative

en: Jump and sing about the unceasing nectar who
having obstructed the black sea, entered Laṅkā
[and] cutting off the one and nine golden crowns
of the ignorant one
gave the vast kingdom to that one’s younger brother
Jump and sing about the king of Ayodhyā!
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, negative, masculine, singular

en: For those who master [these] five and five [verses]
Composed in fine Tamil by Viṭṭucittaṉ
of Putuvai in the south
on the words of the bright ornamented ladies
who played a game of jumping and singing
proclaiming [the stories of] Nanda’s son and Kākutstha
there will be no misfortune
gloss: play game of jumping and singing

en: Lady with curly dark tresses! Salutations! I am your servant
[He] broke the bow of Janaka, with a crown crowded with jewels
knowing that [he would] attain you
and, having taken the thick bow in order to obstruct
the way of the one with rare tapas who robbed the kings
[he] destroyed [that] tapas
This is one proof
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Lady with a lovely water-lily flower blossom garland!
I bow at [your] feet. Salutations!
Graciously hear me speak
you gentle doe with a pair of blossom eyes!
Sweetly waiting patiently in a solitary place at dusk
[and] binding [Him] there with an auspicious garland of jasmine
This is one proof
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, vocative, second person

en: When Kaikeyī, with a greatly agitated mind, asked for a boon
[and] the king, with a mind very bewildered
[realizing] he could not refuse
replied saying, “Noble son, go to dwell in the forest!”
[And] Lakṣmaṇa went there with him
This is one proof
gloss: pronominalised noun, masculine, singular, third person

en: Lady with breasts wrapped in a bodice!
Vaidehī! Salutations
Great goddess of the king of Ayodhyā
adorned with chariots, graciously listen
on the Ganges, [he] accepted a friendship
imbued with excellence, with Guha
skilled with a sharp spear
This is one proof
Lady of soft deer-like gaze! Vaidehī! Salutations!
When, having taken the stoney path to the forest
you dwelt in the forest, You of milk[-sweet] words
on the Citrakūṭa hill-side with honey-filled groves
and Prince Bharata [came and] bowed
This is one proof
While sitting on Cittirakūṭa
a little crow touched [your] breast
so [you] discharged a missile
[which] ran chasing [it] throughout the world
until [it] cried out
“Wise One! Oh Rāmā! [Please give] your refuge!”
and that missile pierced [its] eye
This is one proof
Lady with the lightening thin waist!
I am your true servant, Salutations!
When the golden deer entered [the forest] and played sweetly
in accordance with your wishes
our Lord grasped [his] bow and left
and Lakṣmaṇa departed after [him]
This is one proof
Lady with dark blossoms resembling kohl in [your] tresses!
Vaidevī! Salutations
When [he] thought to search [for you]
along with the king of monkeys of equal fame
the king of Ayodhyā with befitting excellence
spoke of these [incidents as] proof
[But, the most] befitting proof is this, his ring!
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: The day when [he] went to the fire sacrifice of the ruler
whose praise pervades the eight quarters
in the middle of the very big assembly, he broke the bow
Seeing the ring, Sītā, with blossom [filled] tresses
holding [it] high, rejoiced, saying
“This proof is indeed acceptable, Hanuman!”
Those who master the song of the lord and scholar of Putuvai
with glory that fills the earth
[about] the proof that was known and
by brave and virtuous Hanuman
told to Vaidevī, the simple woman with bodiced breasts
when [he] saw her
Will live with the celestials in beautiful Vaikuntha
If you seek the dwelling place of Rāmā
with uncontested greatness
he with the tall crown that burns like the rays of a thousand suns
there are those who have truly seen him as a lion
tearing open the chest of Hiraṇya
with warring shoulders and shaking anklets
with hands covered with blood
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, accusative, perfective aspect
participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

en: If you seek the dwelling place of Rama
with the greatness of bearing the Nāndaka [sword]
the conch, the staff, the Śārṅga with resounding bowstring
and the divine discus
there are those who have seen him at the sacrifice
of King Janaka, king of kings
[where he] went to break the strong bow for the sake of Sītā
[her] fingers like the buds of glory lilies
gloss: participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

en: If you tenaciously seek the deity
who plucked out the tusk of the murderous elephant
engaged in battle so that the enemy army was ruined
[and] shot arrows with [his] bow at the fig tree
there are those who have seen the place where he sits
in splendour on the seashore spread over with waves
[while] monkey troops come, bearing upon [their] heads
huge mountains to obstruct [the sea]
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, accusative, perfective aspect
participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

en: If [you] seek the wondrous babe who took an ancient form
in the midst of the surrounding vast waters
come! I’ll give you a hint
There are those who truly saw him standing
angrily fighting the seven battle-bulls so that they died
for the sake of the simple cowherd woman, Piṉṉai
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person
participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

en: If you seek Tirumāl who remained when
he with the blue throat and red matted locks
from which waters rise
and the four-faced one performed words of praise
abounding in excellence by turns
there are those who certainly saw him when
doing battle in the midst of the army
[he] forcefully seized and took Rukmiṇī
with breast swelling from [her] bodice
[and] put [her] in [his] chariot
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

en: If you are seeking the place where appears
the dark jewel hued one who placed his mouth
to the breast of the demoness of evil form
and was able to drink so that [she] died
there are those who saw him seated on the lion throne
in Dvarakā while the ocean rose
and all others, along with many thousands of great goddesses
surrounded [him]
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, singular, masculine, accusative, perfective aspect
participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

en: If you ask for the place where appears him with hands
that bear the sounding white conch
and the fiery, bright, divine discus
come, I with give you a tiny hint
There are those who saw [him] standing
at the front of [his] chariot with a white horse
and a monkey victory banner
when, as a sly friend to the army
[he] lent [his] hand to the Bhārata war
gloss: participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

en: The child of Devakī
who fought with weapons so that the hours passed
in front of the kings who stood guard hour after hour
there are those who saw [him]
at the side of he who fought with weapons
when [he] hid the sun with [his] discus that day
so that Jayadratha’s head rolled into the waste land
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect
participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

en: If you are consistently seeking the deity
who swallowed whole the earth, the mountains
the crashing seas and all else, [and then] spit [them] out
there are those who saw the one
as an inconceivably rare boar
pierced and dug out the vast earth
who married the beautiful, dark haired lady
gloss: negative, participial noun, masculine, singular, dative
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, accusative
participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

ta: பரவு மனமுடைப் பத்தருள் ளார்பர மனடிசேர் வர்களே
en: Those who are devotees with hearts that praise [this]
garland of ten [verses] composed by the lord scholar learned
in the Veda, in which prosperity flourishes
in Putuvai with paddy fields that produce red paddy
rising high [like] the heads of horses
giving hints for seeing Māyaṉ
with a body that resembles a black cloud
they will reach with the feet of the Supreme
The mountain of the king who stands as a lamp to [his] clan
having caused devastation to the clan of demons
who wandered about terrifying and killing
is Tirumāliruñcōlai in the South where flows the Cilampu river
with the sound of dancing celestial ladies
coming loudly from [their] tinkling anklets
The mountain where dwells
he who cut off the arms of the strong one
the heads of the sword[-bearing] demon
[and] the nose of the evil younger sister
is Tirumāliruñcōlai in the South of spreading fame
where “Many years” resounds
pervading everywhere, in every place
gloss: causative, perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular

en: The golden mountain of the wealthy Lord
who sent on the path to hell the ferocious [demons]
who caused [both] virtuous and the excellent men grief
is cool Tirumāliruñcōlai where that wilderness path
is transformed for devotees who
are always going and serving [the Lord]
gloss: participial noun, third person, perfective aspect
participial noun, third person, plural, accusative

en: The mountain of he who lifted Govardhana
to stop the festival for the king of immortals
that was celebrated by the assembled cow herders
is Tirumāliruñcōlai in the South where a river of honey flows
falling from the huge flower clusters of the Kaṟpaka [tree]
standing in the heavenly country
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect

en: The mountain where comes and dwells
the one who took in service one elephant in a pond
[and] consumed the life of Kaṃsa’s elephant
is cool Tirumāliruñcōlai where wanders a dark elephant
foresaking its mate when it fled
in order to utter a holy vow to the sea-hued One
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: The mountain of him with four arms annointed with sandal paste
who smashed the wrestlers who came against [him]
in accordance with [the wishes of] he who gave the orders
so that [they] died
is Tirumāliruñcōlai in the South where immortals and good sages
serve [him], saying “Succor in [times of] adversity”
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, third person, neuter plural
participial noun, singular, masculine, imperfective aspect

en: The mountain of him who drew subterranean water
standing there long ago on a chariot for [his] cousins
in order to bewilder the [enemy] kings
is Tirumāliruñcōlai in the South, praised by the southern King
King of Kūṭal in the South, Neṭumāṟaṉ
king with a sharp spear, practiced in killing
gloss: causative, perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular

en: The golden mountain of the wealthy Lord who
having destroyed the lairs of the lesser kings
drove [them] onto the narrow footpaths
in the middle of the hot jungle
is Tirumāliruñcōlai in the South where six-legged striped bees
sing [his] thousand names in the early dawn
The mountain of [our] father that gives succor in [times of] adversity
as demons gather up the red blood that scatters and swells
giving [it] as an offering at dusk
is Tirumāliruñcōlai in the South
where Indragōpa beetles spill out through the forest
so that they resemble the ripe fruit lips of our lord
The mountain where the immaculate One is majestically enthroned
while countless great goddesses shine
emitting [light] to the eight directions
is Tirumāliruñcōlai in the south where unbridled female elephants
gone sniffing [out] the bulls
Sway to and fro, rubbing against [them] in the evening
Those who meditatively recite the words of Viṭṭucittaṉ
[who dwells in] Villiputtūr
where, having taken a vow, he praised
the lord of dark ocean hue, who dwells intentionally
[on] the mountain of Māliruñcōlai
adorned with maruta groves
they will see Kaṇṇaṉ’s pair of anklets
gloss: participial noun, third person, imperfective aspect

en: The mountain of him who rebuked and disgraced Rukmaṉ
who went running after [him]
in order to return the lady Rukmiṇī
[and] drove [him] off
that is the vast Māliruñcōlai where the Koṉṟai tree
standing on the mountain
lovingly gives golden rings and coins of leaves
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular

en: The mountain of the sapphire-hued One who grew to destroy
Kaṃsa, Kāḷiya, the elephant, the Marutu trees
and the bull through deceit
that is Tirumāliruñcōlai where the venom spitting serpent rises
coming near, to steal the huge, cool moon
with [its] fiery red tongue
The mountain of the sea-hued One who, having gone to surround
the resident of hell, seized and destroyed [him]
carried off the virgin ladies
that is Māliruñcōlai with groves surrounded by golden necklaces
of Puṉṉai, Cerunti, upland Vēṅkai, and Kōṅku trees
The mountain that is desired by the solitary young man
who destroyed the prison where sat the son of Mahābali
and the daughter of Bāṇa
that is Māliruñcōlai where women of the hill country perform
singing the sounds of melodious kuṟiñci verses
and dancing [in praise] of Govinda of the herders
The mountain of the ornamented lord, the handsome one
who stopped the babbling of Śiśupāla who ridiculed [him]
uttering many, many abuses
that is Tirumāliruñcōlai, the noble mountain
the beautiful mountain, the huge, cool mountain
the victory mountain, the earth mountain
the tall mountain
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: The mountain of [our] father who, in that very time and place
placed upon the wives of the hundred
all the distress of Pāñcāli, [wife] of the Pāṇḍavas
that is ancient Māliruñcōlai
the mountain that has deep spring wells
so that swarms of bees, worthy of song
sing melodies and drink honey
The mountain of our strong armed Rāma who
having spread arrows
for the sake of the lady with the gold earring
raised the family of demons on stakes
that is beautiful Māliruñcōlai where
a gathering of multitudes from the whole of the broad earth
come to bathe, surrounding the clear waterfalls that cast gold ashore
The mountain where abides the king who was satisfied
having dispelled the complete crookedness of Laṅkā
with fire spitting arrows rained down from the tip of his stripped bow
the mountain where the king along with the celestials
[and] the wandering sun and moon go to cirucumambulate
that is Tirumāliruñcōlai!
The mountain of the spotless one who played at
digging up and taking the earth with [his] tusks
measuring and taking the earth in the palm of [his] hand
[and] consuming and spitting it out again
that is Māliruñcōlai with the cool Cilampu River
which comes running with offerings
of many gathered treasures for our Lord
The mountain where reigns he whose bed is Aṉanta
with a thousand green heads
as [his] thousand arms spread [wide]
[and his] thousand crowns glitter [like] lightning
that is Māliruñcōlai with a thousand flower groves
a thousand rivers, and many thousand mountain springs!
The mountain [like Lord] who has [as his place]
the mountain called Māliruñcōlai
he with the four eminent forms
the nectar of the ocean of the four Vedas
the heavenly Kaṟpaka tree
the heavenly light on the highest meaning of the Vedānta
these have been expounded by Viṭṭucittaṉ
In Tirukkōṭṭiyūr dwell those whose tongues
never speak of evil acts [and]
those who maintian the feast each day
repeating the Vedas and performing virtuous deeds
Why did the Creator create those sinners
who do not think of the First Cause Lord
who rectifies the deeds of the three?
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person
participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect
singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect

en: In Tirukkōṭṭiyūr dwell those with generous hands
who are without hatred for anything
being blessings to the gurus
increasing [their] faultless excellence
[and] there are those who do not worship him
with the pure jewel hue, who seized the seven worlds
with [his] mouth and consumed [them]
who were born to cause great suffering
to the bellies of the mothers who begot [them]
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, third person, plural

en: In Tirukkōṭṭiyūr, surrounded by verandas erected in the shade
inlaid with emeralds and sapphire of fine hue
there are those who
with the fingers used to count the holy names of Tirumāl
go [about] unable to think [of His names] for even an instant
use [them] to eat, pushing rice balls into their filthy mouths
gloss: present tense, participial noun, third person, plural

en: In Tirukkōṭṭiyūr with red lotus fields
where flocks of simple swans
[each looking] like the conch that resides
in the hand of he with the soft serpent bed
fly up [and] spread out
there is a caste of men who do not call out “Hell Destroyer”
with [their] tongues
[even] the water [they] drink and the clothes [they] wear
are committing sins, are they not?
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: In Tirukkōṭṭiyūr with waters where play
the young Vāḷai fish who engage in mischief
going about, leaping on the backs of tortoises
bending white flowers to and fro
[there are those who are a] burden to the earth
having a hard heart, never thinking of him
with the broad, discus laden hand
remove the food [they are] eating
and stuff grass [in their mouths instead]!
In Tirukkōṭṭiyūr dwell those with generous hands
without a single flaw [occuring] with the five elements
five sacrifices, five senses, and five sense organs
this earth experiences the fortune of bearing the dust
on the feet that is stirred up by those who praise
saying “Nātha!” “Narasiṃha!”
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, third person, plural

en: In Tirukkōṭṭiyūr dwell those of the four perfect vedas
praising day and night, celebrating the festivals
and going, joining, [and] dancing
with him who broke the wild lime tree
What penance has been performed
by the people who inhabit this city
where devotees join [their] hands in worship
to him with the hue of a broad, dark cloud?
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, sociative
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

en: In Tirukkōṭṭiyūr red-eyed Māl receives service each day
from he of a pleasant nature, he of unwavering rectitude
from he of lofty affection, and effulgent prosperity
Even demons are unable to steal much ripened grain
in [this] country where Govinda dwells happliy
with those who sing of [his] qualities
In Tirukkōṭṭiyūr with fertile fields surrounded
by walls made of superior red gold
where cuckoo flocks in groves fill the branches
singing of the qualities of Govinda
if [I] see those who praise [Him], saying “Nampaṉ” “Narasiṃha”
thinking, “All of these people are signs of our Lord,”
I will have ended [my] longings
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, third person, plural, accusative

en: In Tirukkōṭṭiyūr dwell those of generous hands
who receive words of praise
giving rice without trade or concealment
even though a hand[ful] could be sold for gold
Those who say “Keśava!”, “Puruṣottama!”, “Shining Light!”, “Dwarf!”
are servants who get to sell us
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, vocative, second person
participial noun, third person, imperfective aspect

en: Those who flawlessly pronounce the words of
Viṭṭucittaṉ, King of cool Putuvai, Lord of faultless scholars
about those who are devotees of the Primal Lord
and those who wander without serving [the Lord]
in Tirukkōṭṭiyūr with fertile fields
surrounded on [all] sides by cool waters
are servants of Hṛṣīkeśa
gloss: negative, participial noun, third person, accusative
imperfective aspect, participial noun, third person, plural

en: Those with minds that cling to desire, on the edge of death
[if,] being confused, they do not call out
“Mother! Father! My sons! My Land!
Lady with fragrance filled locks!”
[but] say “Keśava! Puruṣottama!
Imperishable One who became a boar!”
—if speaking of the greatness that they attain
it is not [within] our power
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, vocative, second person
participial noun, third person, imperfective aspect

en: Before going and reaching the edge [of death]
being maddened by itching because of flies
maggots spreading and mingling on raised sores
thick with pus everywhere
if [you] go, joining [your] hands in worship atop [your] head
[and] saying with [your] mouth, “Namo Nāraṇa”
afterward, even if given a guarantee
of perpetually [returning] to this place
He will not allow [you] to go
gloss: verbal noun, participial noun, masculine, singular

en: Before reaching the time [of death]
if they question [you] on all sides
saying “If [you have] hoarded stolen wealth
tell [us]! Tell [us]!”
without even opening [your] mouth
building a temple in [your] heart
establish the god called Mādhava [there]
For those who are able to give the flower called love
there is escape from the punishment of Yama
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

en: Before the last rising breath is expelled
the windpipe ceases to function
the arms and legs are possessed
by trembling and shaking
and the eyes sleep [forever]-
before that happens
take in the three measures of the one letter
that is the Cause so that [your] heart swells
if you love the sea-hued Lord
[your] dwelling place will be in heaven
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, perfective aspect, second person, plural

en: As piss trickles through [your] clothes
[your] throat closes so that conjee
poured in [your] mouth, passing through
dribbles from [your] lips
and [your] eyes sleep [forever]
before that happens
you are able to praises Hṛṣīkeśa
so that dogs do not bite at your thighs
they do not leap at you with tridents
and you do not lose the clothes at [your] waist
For those who adhere to one act
placing and firmly establishing in [their] hearts
Matucūtaṉaṉ, Māyaṉ
whose bed is in the sea where ships roam
before the five senses, expelled, abandon the body
[and] after testing the nose for breath
the assembly leaves
waving their hands and
lowly lowering [their] heads
[they] will persist forever
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, third person, dative

en: [If you are] looking to end the darkness in [your] heart
thinking [of him], saying “He is such a One”
before the crooked servants of Yama
come like those who drive oxen
kicking and tying [you] up with strong rope
and then dragging [you] back and forth
—[take note that] those who say “King Madhusūdana”
are the intermediaries of heaven
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person
participial noun, third person, imperfective aspect

en: Before [your] relatives congregate
speaking of [your] virtues and leaving aside [your] faults
singing as [they] place [you] on a bier
and cover [you] with cloth like a gift for a fox troop
[take note that,] because the ones with hearts that dance
join with Govinda who has the Kaustubha jewel
they will escape, passing over the place [Yama] intended
While prattling on
pain throbing on one side of the mouth
mucous increasing
[and] eyes hollowed out
[your] mother on one side, father on one side
[your] wife babbling incessently on another side
before the fire reaches the [last] side
[take note that] for those who are able to remain on one side as relatives
who have entanglements with red-eyed Māl
they will escape the punishment of Yama
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, neuter plural

en: Those who master this garland of ten composed about Tirumāl
by the king of Puttūr, strong armed Viṭṭucittaṉ
having concentrated [his] mind well
about the blessing attained by those who die as devotees to the Lord of gods
and the deeds of those who think of [Him] at the time of death
they are those who, having concentrated [their] minds well
obtain thoughts that dwell on Tirumāl
gloss: participial noun, third person, perfective aspect

en: You fools who give [your children] useless names
because of desire for stained clothes, coins
and a handful of grain!
Give the name Kesava [and] you will be happy!
The mother of [a] Nāyaka Nāraṇa will not go to hell
gloss: pronominalised noun, plural, third person, vocative

en: Fools give the names of the decaying human species
[to your children] because of the desire to wear a loin cloth
Ladies! [But] if [you] call out, “Red Eyed Tall Māl! Śrīdhara!”
the mother of Nāraṇa will not go to hell
gloss: pronominalised noun, plural, third person, vocative

en: You who swell with waste
hankering after sesame oil and ornaments
for your head and bangles [for your arms]!
Why do you give other names?
Even if coming for alms, mutter the holy names of our Lord!
The mother of Nāraṇa will not go to hell
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, second person, vocative

en: If one gives a human name to a human being
born to the human species
there is no [going] to the next world
If calling out “Govinda! Mādhava who possesses heaven!”
the mother of Nāraṇa, who rules me
will not go to hell
If one gives the name of the filth of excrement
to the filth of excrement
born in the filth of excrement
there is no [going] to the next world
If calling out “Noble Govinda! Govinda!”
the mother of virtuous Nāraṇa will not go to hell
Don’t give the name of a man
such that it is known in city and country
and fall down and suffer in the pit along with [him]
without escape
seek [Him instead]
saying “Leader who lept to break the cart! Dāmodara!”
The mother of Nāraṇa will not go to hell
O Foolish men who, having been born in this world
[and] giving the names of humans born in this world
[to your children]
without a single thought for the next world!
Adhere to the names of the dark cloud hued [Lord]
pleasing to the eye
The mother of Nāraṇa will not go to hell

ta: நம்பி பிம்பியென் று நாட் டுமானிடப் பேரிட்டால்
en: If [one] gives the name of a man from the country
[like] Nambi or Pimbi
all the Nampis and Pimpis will vanish
having been dispensed with on [merely] the count of four!
If, [however,] having given the name
[you] call out Kaṇṇaṉ, with the big, red lotus [eyes]
O Nampis, the mother of Nāraṇa will not go to hell
Giving the name of my could hued [lord]
to [your] piss [soaked] child
[it’s] as if you are pouring ambrosia into a pit of filth
Come together, join hands and whirl about in a riotous dance!
The mother of Nāraṇa, with [a name] worthy of the tongue
will not go to hell
Those who master these one and nine
unique, effulgent Tamil [verses]
composed by Viṣṇucitta of ancient
fame dressed in heroism
that make clear to give the holy names of Māl
adorned in perfection
they with be forever esteemed in Vaikuntha of vast beauty

ta: தங்கையை மூக்குந் தமையனைத் தலையுந் தடிந்தவெந் தாசர திபோ
யெங்குந்தன் புகழா விருந்தர சாண்ட வெம்புரு டோ த்தம னிருக்கை
கங்கைகங் கையென் றவாசகத் தாலே கடுவினை களைந்திட கிற்குங்
கங்கையின் கரைமேல் கைதொழ நின்ற கண்டமென் னுங்கடி நகரே
en: The residence of our Puruṣottama
who rules [his] kingdom being praised everywhere
[who] came to us as Dāśarathi who cut off the nose of the younger sister
and the head of the older bother
is the protected city called Kaṇṭam
where [he] stands to be worshipped with joined hands
on the banks of the Ganges
exterminating painful karma with the words, “Ganges Ganges”

ta: சலம்பொதி யுடம்பின் தழலுமிழ் பேழ்வாய்ச் சந்திரன் வெங்கதி ரஞ்ச
மலர்ந்தெழுந் தணவு மணிவண்ண வுருவின் மால்புரு டோத்தமன் வாழ்வு
நலந்திகழ் சடையான் முடிக்கொன்றை மலரும் நாரணன் பாதத்து ழாயுங்
கலந்திழி புனலால் புகர்படு கங்கைக் கண்டமென் னுங்கடி நகரே
en: The residence of Māl Puruṣottama
whose jewel-toned form arose and bloomed
approaching so that [he] frightened the moon
with a body that stores water
