and the hot sun with a maw that spits fire
is the protected city called Kaṇṭam
[on the banks] of the beautiful Ganges
with waters that fall
mixing the koṉṟai blossoms
from the head of [Śiva’s] red, shining, matted locks
[with] the tulasi from the feet of Nāraṇa
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

ta: அதிர்முக முடைய வலம்புரி குமிழ்த்தி யழலுமி ழாழிகொண் டெறிந்தங்
கெதிர்முக வசுரர் தலைகளை யிடறு மெம்புரு டோத்தம னிருக்கை
சதுமுகன் கையில் சதுப்புயன் தாளில் சங்கரன் சடையினில் தங்கி
கதிர்முக மணிகொண் டிழிபுனல் கங்கைக் கண்டமென் னுங்கடி நகரே
en: The residence of our Puruṣottama
who, at one time, blew the conch with a thunderous mouth
grabbed and threw [his] fire-spitting discus
[and] struck the heads of the demon [he] faced in battle
is the protected city called Kaṇṭam [on the banks] of the Ganges
[where] waters descend with brilliant jewels
from the hands of the four-faced [Brahmā]
the feet of the four-armed [Viṣṇu]
[and] the matted locks of Śaṅkara

ta: இமையவ ரிறுமாந் திருந்தர சாளவேற் றுவந்தெ திர்பொரு சேனை
நமபுரம் நணுக நாந்தகம் விசிறும் நம்புரு டோத்தமன் நகர்தா
னிமவந்தந் தொடங்கி யிருங்கட லளவு மிருகரை யுலகிரைத் தாட
கமையுடைப் பெருமைக் கங்கையின் கரைமேல் கண்டமென் னுங்கடி நகரே
en: The city of our Puruṣottama
who weilded Nāndaka to send to Yama’s city
the army that fought, coming en masse, in opposition
when the haughty immortals ruled the realm
is the protected city called Kaṇṭam
on the banks of the Ganges of enduring greatness
[where] the [whole] world [comes] to bathe, shouting
on [its] two shores, from the Himalayas to the vast ocean

ta: உழுவதோர் படையு முலக்கையும் வில்லு மொண்சுட ராழியுஞ் சங்கும்
மழுவொடு வாளும் படைக்கல முடைய மால்புரு டோத்தமன் வாழ்
வெழுமை யுங்கூடி யீண்டிய பாவ மிறைப்பொழு தளவினி லெல்லாங்
கழுவிடும் பெருமைக் கங்கையின் கரைமேல் கண்டமென் னுங்கடி நகரே
en: The dwelling place of Māl Puruṣottama
armed with [an array of] weapons
a sword, along with an axe
a tool for ploughing, the pestle, bow
bright flaming discus, and conch
is the protected city called Kaṇṭam
on the banks of the great Ganges
where all the sins collected and clustered over seven births
are removed in an instant

ta: தலைப்பெய்து குமுறிச் சலம்பொதி மேகஞ் சலசல பொழிந்திடக் கண்டு
மலைப்பெருங் குடையால் மறைத்தவன் மதுரை மால்புரு டோத்தமன் வாழ்
வலைப்புடைத் திரைவா யருந்தவ முனிவ ரவபிர தங்குடைந் தாட
கலப்பைகள் கொழிக்குங் கங்கையின் கரைமேல் கண்டமென் னுங்கடி நகரே
en: The dwelling place of Māl Puruṣottama
who, seeing the cloud filled with water
as a torrential downpour [began] overhead
resounding with the sound of pattering [rain]
protected Madurai with a huge umbrella [made of a] mountain
is the protected city called Kaṇṭam
on the banks of the Ganges where ploughs are cast ashore
as sages practice difficult austerities
[and] plunge into the waves that ebb and flow
for [their] ritual ablutions
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular

ta: விற்பிடித் திறுத்து வேழத்தை முருக்கி மேலிருந் தவன்தலை சாடி
மற்பொரு தெழப்பாய்ந் தரையனை யுதைத்த மால்புரு டோத்தமன் வாழ்
வற்புத முடையை ராவத மதமு மவரிளம் படியரொண் சாந்துங்
கற்பக மலருங் கலந்திழி கங்கைக் கண்டமென் னுங்கடி நகரே
en: The dwelling of Māl Puruṣottama
who grabbed and broke the bow, crushed the elephant
[and] beat the head of the one who sat atop [it]
Lept up to fight the wrestlers, and kicked the king
is the protected city called Kaṇṭam on the Ganges
which descends, mixing the blossoms of the Kaṟpaka tree
[with] the ichor of Indra’s marvelous elephant
[and] the bright sandal paste [worn by] his damsels
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

ta: திரைபொரு கடல்சூழ் திண்மதிள் துவரை வேந்து தன் மைத்துனன் மார்க்காய்
அரசினை யவிய வரசினை யருளு மரிபுரு டோ த்தம னமர்வு
நிரைநிரை யாக நெடியன யூபம் நிரந்தர மொழுக்குவிட் டிரண்டு
கரைபுரை வேள்விப் புகைகமழ் கங்கை கண்டமென் னுங்கடி நகரே
en: The abode of Hari Puruṣottama
who, as king of strong walled Dvārakā
surrounded by a sea of crashing waves
when the kings were defeated
granted the kingdom to his cousins
is the protected city called Kaṇṭam
on the ganges where the fragrant smoke
of sacrificial fires spreads
the two banks resembling the tall sacrificial posts row on row
[from which smoke] emits, flowing endlessly

ta: வடதிசை மதுரை சாளகி ராமம் வைகுந்தந் துவரைய யோத்தி
யிடமுடை வதரி யிடவகை யுடைய வெம்புரு டோ த்தம னிருக்கை
தடவரை யதிரத் தரணிவிண் டிடியத் தலைப்பற்றிக் கரைமரஞ் சாடி
கடலினைக் கலங்கக் கடுத்திழி கங்கைக் கண்டமென் னுங்கடி நகரே
en: The seat of our Puruṣottama
who has the places of Madura in the North
Śālagrāma, Vaikuntha, Dvārakā, [and] Ayodhyā
[and] places like Badarī
is the protected city called Kaṇṭam
on the Ganges which descends swiflty to agitate the sea
splitting the earth so [it] crumbles
[and] the broad mountains shake
seizing the tops [and] breaking the shore trees

ta: மூன்றெழுத் ததனை மூன்றெழுத் ததனால் மூன்றெழுத் தாக்கிமூன் றெழுத்தை
யேன்றுகொண் டிருப்பார்க் கிரக்கநன் குடைய வெம்புரு டோ த்தம னிருக்கை
மூன்றடி நிமிர்த்து மூன்றினில் தோன்றி மூன்றினில் மூன்றுரு வானான்
கான்தடம் பொழில்சூழ் கங்கையின் கரைமேல் கண்டமென் னுங்கடி நகரே
en: The seat of our Puruṣottama
having the goodness of grace for
those who accept the three letters
the three letters having created
the three letters with the three letters
is the protected city called Kaṇṭam on the banks of the Ganges
surrounded by huge forested groves
of him who took three steps, appeared in the three
[and] took the form of the three in the three
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, third person, dative

ta: பொங்கொலி கங்கைக் கரைமலி கண்டத் துறைபுரு டோ த்தம னடிமேல்
வெங்கலி நலியா வில்லிபுத் தூர்க்கோன் விட்டுசித் தன்விருப் புற்று
தங்கிய வன்பால் செய்ததமிழ் மாலை தங்கிய நாவுடை யார்க்கு
கங்கையில் திருமால் கழலிணைக் கீழே குளித்திருந் தகணக் காமே
en: For those with tongues that remain on [this] Tamil garland
composed with abiding loveby Viṭṭucittaṉ, king of Villiputtūr
[a city] that does not suffer from cruel calamities
feeling [great] longing for the feet of Puruṣottama who resides in Kaṇṭam
rising on the banks of the roiling, roaring Ganges
the result will be bathing beneath Tirumāl’s ankleted pair of feet in the Ganges
The city of him who gave the son of the ascetic
who had died after entering the swelling sea
his true form as a teaching gift
is called Araṅkam
with waters that pour forth honey contained in flower buds
that, when men of the pure Vedas [with] clean vestments
bathe in the river, overflows in every direction
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, accusative
singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect

en: The city where dwells he who retrieved
and immediately reunited the four children
who had died in the birthing room
is called holy Araṅkam, where live eminent men of the Vedas
who maintain the great Vedic fire
and are gracious to guests
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, imperfective aspect
third person, participial noun, imperfective aspect
third person, participial noun, imperfective aspect

en: The city of him who, with the face of a guru
restored the life of his nephew’s son
[and] rescued the bodies of [his] cousins
[from] dying in a sacrifice
is called Araṅkam
with waters where bloom, standing face to face
red lotuses like [his] holy face
[and] dark blue water-lilies like [his] holy body
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: The city of him who
upon hearing the harsh words
from the mouth the cruel woman
that had been spoken by [her] sinful humpback slave
left [his] kingdom and the mother who bore and raised [him]
[and] having taken the dense forest path
exterminated the Kaṇṭakas
is called holy Araṅkam with groves
[full of] blossoms heavy with honey
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, feminine, third person
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular

en: The city of he who secured the protection of this world
having utterly destroyed in battle
the body of villanous Rāvaṇa
[who had] obtained great boons
is called holy Araṅkam, the place associated with my Tirumāl
surrounded by cool groves where Cuckoos cry out
while blue Kuravu flowers bud
and red Kōṅku trees blossom
gloss: causative, perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular

en: The city of the destroyer who
having dispatched [his] discus
exterminated the demons in the underworld
[even right down to] their unborn
not even being able to arise
is Araṅkam where groups of bees, adorned with white pollen
rubbing between the leaves of the screw-pine
create a tune [like] the sweet sound of the Yāḻ
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular

en: The city of Perumāṉ who made corpses of villanous demons
such that [their] blood, abundant with flesh and fat
bubbled up [and] showered down
is beautiful Araṅkam where the roaring Kāveri
comes worshipping [his] feet
carrying along Sandal trees from the vast mountains
[so big they are] difficult to embrace
The city of him who
as a strong tusked boar [and] a sharp toothed lion
dug out the limitless earth and the [chest of] the demon
is called walled Araṅkam
where in the evening huge winged beetles sing
[about] the virtues of our Perumāṉ
[and] play the white conch[-like] Jasmine
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: The city of Neṭumāl whose complexion is
like a flock of dancing peacocks
like the fertile clouds that dance [around] the hills
like the Kuvaḷai flowers and the roaring sea
is called walled Araṅkam
where the south wind [blows] at the crossroads
creeps through hill and grove
[and] embraced the breasts of ladies with creeper[-thin] waists
We are servants to those who are able to praise him
who burned the two bodies
with [this] Tamil garland [about] holy Araṅkam
compsed by Viṭṭucittaṉ
on the divine ruler of Tiruppati
who fought the one who, have obtained great boons
arose, roaring in battle,[and] oblitereated [him]
so that he was destroyed in battle
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, accusative
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, accusative

en: The temple of Tirumāl who
having gone to give [his] wooden sandal
to [his] younger brother as a heavenly pledge
[and] having come to perfectly perform [his] duty
in the place of battle so that the celestials lived
rules the world
is bright Araṅkam, where the wind shakes [and] moves
the beautiful blue flowers, oho!
revealing [his] divine feet and body
[and] the flower eye of [his] divine lady
Even though the Lady of the Lotus speaks of the faults
in the conduct of his servants
it is as if he will say, “My servants would not do that
even if [they] did, they did it for good”
They serve no other but he of holy Araṅkam, my [Lord]
where [he has] placed his blossom eyes
looking in the direction of walled Laṅkā
for the sake of princely Vibhīṣaṇa
Having appeared in order to destroy
the Marutu trees in the dark grove
the angry elephant, Pralamba, the cruel horse
the [demon disguised as] the wheeled cart
and the wrestlers
He heard cheers
The city where dwells he who
raising [his] servants up through
the realm of the fiery sun that dispells the darkness
removing the ladder, and bestowing grace [upon them]
accepts [them] as servants
is beautiful Araṅkam
The eternal temple of the bridegroom
who sits majestically as king
in that [place] called Dvārakā
while 16,000 queens do [him] service
is [in] Araṅkam on the water
where the fresh lotus flowers stand tall
contemplating [his]universal sovereignty
such that [they are] equal to the blossom
in the golden navel of our Lord
[and] bend [to give their] golden [pollen]
The temple of him who reclines while joyful Nārada
again and again prostrates and praises
Him who became the turtle, the Ganges
the deep sea, the earth, the great mountains
the four-faced [Brahmā], the four Vedas
the sacrifices, and the offerings
is in Araṅkam on the water
where flocks of birds come together on flowers
[and] sing the praises of the bird-king
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: The temple where dwells the ruler of [our] lives
who took and rescued Uttarā’s boy
[and] made [his] cousins kings
[so that] their wife was able to tie up [her] hair
is in holy Araṅkam which stands as a lamp to [all] directions
as bhaktas, bhagavas, sages [learned] in the ancient words
the [entire] vast country, and the siddhas
[all] prostrate, worshipping [him]
The temple of our Lord who was pleased
having, as a dwarf brahmācārya
overcame the power of Māvali
took [his] kingdom, [and] in an instant
gave [him] hell as a home
is holy Araṅkam where beautiful jewels shine
on the lustrous hoods of [his] serpent bed
as if the morning sun rose on radiant jewelled mountain
The temple of him who, with mouth wide, roared
when, having grasped [his] chest
[he] crushed the bright chest of Hiraṇya
with the tips of [his] claws
[and] clutching [his] head
[he] squeezed so that [his] crown broke
and [his] eyes bulged out
is cool Araṅkam where
while fertilized lotus blossoms appear
rising like the red feet that measured the worlds
the red paddy with grain that was planted in ridges
bend their stalks [as if] bending [their] heads
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular

en: The temple of him who became the divine fish
tortoise, boar, lion, dwarf, [and] the three
Rāma, Kaṇṇaṉ, and ending with Kalki
is in Araṅkam on the waters
where male and female swans mount red lotus flowers
swinging and dancing
[and] crowd [together] on a flower bed
bathing and playing in the spreading red pollen
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Master of the bird who dominates in battle, master of the earth
master of the one called Nāndaka that does battle
master of the Vedas, master of the undefeated armies
strong armed master, master of darkness, master of the day
master of me
master of [all] the great places of the seven worlds
master of Śrī
holy Araṅkam is where [he] sweetly rests [his] divine eyes
Those who are able to recite [these] Tamil [verses]
composed by Viṭṭucittaṉ, a true servant with a truthful tongue
on the holy city of Araṅkam eternally
praised by the southern and northern regions
[and] the temple favoured by him with the fiery discus
who ended the suffering of the elephant
they will always be united with our Lord’s pair of feet
never to be parted
Is it not the case that resorting to one who has strength
[means that] he will provide protection from all weaknesses?
Even though I am not worthy, I have taken refuge in you
because you granted [your] grace to the elephant
When suffering comes to me, exhausted
I will not be able to think even one thing about you
I have spoken now for that time
Sleeper on the serpent bed in Araṅkam
gloss: verbal noun, neuter singular, imperfective aspect

en: Bearer of the discus and conch
look out for me protectively at the time of death!
The attendants of Yama, tongues curled
will continue inflicting many punishments upon me
At the time of [my] going, nothing at all [of your] virtues
will enter [my mind] to remind [me of] you
only the power of māyā will remain
[Thus] I have spoken about you in the present
Sleeper on the serpent bed in Araṅkam
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
participial noun, neuter singular, imperfective aspect

en: O Bearer of the discus and conch
when, if [I] have reached the entrance to [his] border
Yama’s attendants grab and abuse [me]
there will be no way to say “Stop!”
Whenever [I] could speak, I spoke all your names
take [this as] an indication of my [devotion]
Sleeper on the serpent bed in Araṅkam
[I] need [you] to protect [me], such that [I] do not suffer!
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine, singular, vocative

en: One with [such] greatness that
the one with the bull and the four-faced one do not know you
O First Cause [Lord], did you not become
the entirety of the world and the three letters?
Sleeper on the serpent bed in Araṅkam
on that day [when] Yama’s terrifying attendants
come and grab [me], thinking, “the life of this one is finished”
you must protect me!
Supreme Form who sleeps in the milk ocean
on a hooded serpent bed!
Wanting to create and redeem the world
you birthed the four-faced one in your navel
Knowing that earthly men are unstable
you created Yama together [with them]
O Wonder! Now you must protect me
Sleeper on the serpent bed in Araṅkam
The attendants of Yama, who is without compassion
will continue doing numerous cruelties
You stood, on the other hand, having become earth
water, fire, wind, and ether
Whenever I could think, I thought of all your names
take [that as] an indication of my [devotion]
O Lord! You must protect me
Sleeper on the serpent bed in Araṅkam
Ruler of the gods who remains
as the meaning of the Veda of perfect words! Our Lord!
My faultless sweet nectar!
You who possess the seven worlds! My Father!
When Yama’s attendants with deceptive forms
grab me, compel me and afflict me
saying “don’t fear,” you must protect me
Sleeper on the serpent bed in Araṅkam!
gloss: participial noun, singular, vocative, second person

en: I know nothing of your mysteries
When Yama’s attendants grab and afflict [me]
[and] Strike [me] saying, “Enter this flesh!”
I will be unable to think about you at all
Lord of the celestials fit for heaven!
Great Māyaṉ born in Mathura!
My Elephant! You must protect me
Sleeper on the serpent bed in Araṅkam
Cowherd who protected the cow herd
by lifting up a mountain!
You who grazed the cow herd! Our Lord!
From the first day to this last day
I have never forgotten [your]
ancient, extrordinary splendour
When Yama’s extremely cruel attendants afflict
compel, and seize me
then and there you must protect me
Sleeper on the serpent bed in Araṅkam
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative

en: Those who, being of pure heart
master [this] garland of ten
composed by Viṭṭucittaṉ, king of Villiputtūr
praised by the Vēyar
about Māyavaṉ, Madhusūdana, Mādava
bull of the herder [clan] praised by Vedics
Acyuta, Sleeper on the serpent bed in Araṅkam
they are servants to the pure, jewel-hued One
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, dative, third person

en: Because [my] speech is impure, Mādhava
[my] mouth is unable to grasp you
[But my] tongue knows nothing but you
I fear that is out of my control
Even if [you] become angry, thinking
“this one speaks with arrogance,”
I cannot stop my tongue
Source! One with Garuḍa banner!
Even the declaration from the beak of a crow is fitting
gloss: present tense, third person, masculine, singular

en: One who bears the conch and discus in [your] hands!
With a faulty tongue I have spoken [this] lowly poem
Is it not the duty of the great to endure
the words of their servants, even if they do wrong?
I do not have eyes that look except eyes for you
my mind does not grasp any other
One who ate and spit out the seven worlds long ago
a spot on a deer is not a defect, you see
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, third person
imperfective aspect, third person, noun, singular
participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine, singular, vocative

en: I know nothing of goodness or evils
except this much - to say “Nāraṇā.”
Tirumāl, [this] is not spoken meanly
deceitfully [just] to flatter [you], you see
I know no way to think of you
[So] I say “Namo Nāraṇa” incessantly
Strength, you see, is the strength of the Vaiṣṇava
who lives in your temple
You who measured the seven worlds with your height
Faultless One, Tall One!
Don’t hesitate to take me, your servant, into servitude
Clothes and rice, I have no need for these
With the dignity of that servitude
then and there those will come [to me], you see
You who, by taking the head of the one who bound your father
killing cruel Kaṃsa, liberated [him]
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, vocative
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, vocative, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, accusative, first person
participial noun, neuter singular, imperfective aspect
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative

en: [My] garden, wife, cow, stable, resevoir, fields, and wells
all of these, without fail, I have taken
and apportioned them in a heap at your golden feet
For me it is diffucult to [associate] with earthly men
who have many desires
You who vowed, having become a boar
to take the earth upon [your] tusks!
You who broke the elephant’s tusk so that [it] perished!
gloss: participial noun, third person, imperfective aspect
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative

en: Kṛṣṇa! You who created the four-faced [Brahmā]!
Source! Dark One!
On a day without eating, I, your servant, [feel] no hunger
ceaselessly saying “Namō Nāraṇā”
[but] on days when [I] do not contemplate the
Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas
on days when [I] do not approach your feet with fresh flowers
even if [I] have been afflicted
those days are fasting days for me
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative

en: As [my] hair stands on end, and rejoicing meets sobbing
so that [my] heart languishes with desire
crying out, “is it not possible to see the way that you feign sleep
on that vast serpent bed in the white sea?"
I cannot take to [my] bed to sleep
such that tears trickle from [my] eyes
Tell me the way that I can reach you!
You who held back the rain with a dark mountain
as an umbrella, Madhusūdana!
Kaṇṇaṉ! You who release the elephant from torment!
Source! Lord who conquered the elephant!
You who removes distress from those who contemplate you!
You with fame [so] great it is difficult to praise!
Our Lord, graciously grant [me] the goodness that
being united [with you], I might praise you each day!
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, vocative, perfective aspect
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative
imperfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative

en: Lord of those who, having practised, have mastered [your] praise!
Lord who became the man-lion!
King of celestials! You who measured the seven worlds!
You are the aeons
bearing the discus long ago, you who ended the suffering
of the great, trembling elephant!
[First] Cause! Churner of the sea!
Our Lord, the Nectar who has me as servant!
Remove the distress of this wretch!
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, vocative
participial noun, singular, vocative, second person
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative

en: Those who speak incessantly the names
Father of Kāma, lion to [his] foes
black haired boy [who] is sweet to see
Vāmana, my emerald hued [Lord], Mādhava, Madhusūdana
in these ten Tamil [verses] given by Viṭṭucittaṉ
king of Putuvai where [all] abide in safety and prosperity
[they] will promptly reach the world of Nāraṇaṉ
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, third person, plural

ta: நெய்க்குடத் தைப்பற்றி யேறு மெறும்புகள் போல்நிரந் தெங்குங்
கைக்கொண்டு நிற்கின்ற நோய்காள் காலம் பெறவுய்யப் போமின்
மெய்க்கொண்டு வந்து புகுந்து வேதப் பிரானார் கிடந்தார்
பைக்கொண்ட பாம்பணை யோடும் பண்டன்று பட்டினங் காப்பே
en: O diseases which take hold, spreading everywhere like
ants that swarm a butter pot!
Go! Escape as soon as you can!
The Lord of the Vedas who came and took
[my] body, entering [my heart]!
Unlike before, [this] maritime town is protected by
the one who reclines on a hooded serpent bed
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, third person, vocative

ta: சித்திர குத்தனெ ழுத்தால் தென்புலக் கோன்பொறி யொற்றி
வைத்தவி லச்சினை மாற்றித் தூதுவ ரோடி யொளித்தார்
முத்துத் திரைக்கடற் சேர்ப்பன் மூதறி வாளர் முதல்வன்
பத்தர்க் கமுத னடியேன் பண்டன்று பட்டினங் காப்பே
en: By stamping the letter of the king of the underworld
with Citragupta’s seal
[Yama’s] messengers altered the seal that had been placed
[then] ran away and hid
I am a servant to the chief of the rolling sea [full of] pearls
the Lord of those who master the old knowledge
the nectar of devotees
Unlike before, [this] maritime town has protection

ta: வயிற்றில் தொழுவைப் பிரித்து வன்புலச் சேவை யதக்கி
கயிற்று மக்காணி கழித்துக் காலிடைப் பாசங் கழற்றி
யெயிற்றிடை மண்கொண்ட வெந்தை யிராப்பக லோதுவித் தென்னைப்
பயிற்றிப் பணிசெய்யக் கொண்டான் பண்டன்று பட்டினங் காப்பே
en: Severing the womb in [my] belly
constraining the bull [of my] powerful senses
and removing the sinew and bone [from my] body
undoing the fetters from [my] feet
my father, who took the earth upon [his] tusks
training me, teaching [me] the vedas night and day
takes me to do [his] service
Unlike before, [this] maritime town has protection

ta: மங்கிய வல்வினை நோய்கா ளுமக்குமோர் வல்வினை கண்டீர்
இங்குப் புகேன்மின் புகேன்மி னெளிதன்று கண்டீர் புகேன்மின்
சிங்கப் பிரானவ னெம்மான் சேருந் திருக்கோயில் கண்டீர்
பங்கப் படாதுய்யப் போமின் பண்டன்று பட்டினங் காப்பே
en: Disease of the powerful karma that is death, Look!
There is a powerful karma for you [too]!
Do not enter here! Look!
It’s not easy, do not enter! Do not enter!
Look at [this] holy temple where our king abides
he who is the lion Lord!
Go to be saved without defeat!
Unlike before, [this] maritime town has protection

ta: மாணிக் குறளுரு வாய மாயனை யென்மனத் துள்ளே
பேணிக் கொணர்ந்து புகுத வைத்துக்கொண் டேன்பிறி தின்றி
மாணிக் கப்பண்டா ரங்கண்டீர் வலிவன் குறும்பர்க ளுள்ளீர்
பாணிக்க வேண்டா நடமின் பண்டன்று பட்டினங் காப்பே
en: I took and cherished Māyaṉ as a brahmin dwarf
bringing and placing [him] in my heart
with no other
You who are mighty and very wicked
look at [my] Ruby Treasure!
Go on! There’s no need to wait!
Unlike before, [this] maritime town has protection

ta: உற்ற வுறுபிணி நோய்கா ளுமக்கொன்று சொல்லுகேன் கேண்மின்
பெற்றங்கள் மேய்க்கும் பிரானார் பேணுந் திருக்கோயில் கண்டீர்
அற்ற முரைக்கின்றே னின்ன மாழ்வினை காளுமக் கிங்கோர்
பற்றில்லை கண்டீர் நடமின் பண்டன்று பட்டினங் காப்பே
en: Diseases that cause copious suffering!
Listen, I have something to say to you!
Look at [this] holy temple that adores
the Lord who grazed the cows!
Overwhelming Karma, I will say [this] one more time
Go on! Look! There is nothing here for you to take!
Unlike before, [this] maritime town has protection

ta: கொங்கைச் சிறுவரை யென்னும் பொதும்பினில் வீழ்ந்து வழுக்கி
யங்கோர் முழையினில் புக்கிட் டழுந்திக் கிடந்துழல் வேனை
வங்கக் கடல்வண்ண னம்மான் வல்வினை யாயின மாற்றி
பங்கப் படாவண்ணம் செய்தான் பண்டன்று பட்டினங் காப்பே
en: Having slipped and fallen into a pit
called ‘breasts like little hills,’
I entered a cave there and sunk
staying and wandering about
The Lord, the colour of the ship [laden] sea
having relieved [me of my] powerful karma
made [for me] a path without disgrace
Unlike before, [this] maritime town has protection
gloss: imperfective aspect, participial noun, first person, singular, accusative
singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect

ta: ஏதங் களாயின வெல்லா மிறங்கலி டுவித்தென் னுள்ளே
பீதக வாடைப் பிரானார் பிரம குருவாகி வந்து
போதில் கமலவன் னெஞ்சம் புகுந்து மென்சென்னித் திடரில்
பாத விலச்சினை வைத்தார் பண்டன்று பட்டினங் காப்பே
en: Even though the Lord of golden garments
came as Supreme guru
into my heart, caused all [my] faults to vanish
[and] entered [my] stout lotus heart without leaving
he put the mark of [His] feet upon the top of my head
Unlike before, [this] maritime town has protection

ta: உறக லுறக லுறக லொண்சுட ராழியே சங்கே
யறவெறி நாந்தக வாளே யழகிய சார்ங்கமே தண்டே
யிறவு படாம லிருந்த வெண்ம ருலோகபா லீர்காள்
பறவை யரையா வுறகல் பள்ளி யறைக்குறிக் கோண்மின்
en: Do not sleep! Do not sleep! Do not sleep!
You bright shining disc! Oh conch!
Nāndaka sword that strikes in order to cut!
Beautiful Sārṅga [bow]! Oh staff!
You protectors of the world and the eight [directions]
who are without end!
King of birds! Do not sleep!
Guard [His] bedchamber carefully!

ta: அரவத் தமளியி னோடு மழகிய பாற்கட லோடு
மரவிந்தப் பாவையுந் தானு மகம்படி வந்துபு குந்து
பரவைத் திரைபல மோதப் பள்ளிகொள் கின்றபி ரானை
பரவு கின்றான்விட் டுசித்தன் பட்டினங் காவற் பொருட்டே
en: Viṭṭucittaṉ praises the Lord who sleeps
while many waves crash in the expanse
on [His] serpent bed in the beautiful milk ocean
the Lotus Lady having come and entered [His] heart
because [He] is the protection of [this] maritime town
gloss: present tense, third person, masculine, singular

ta: துக்கச் சுழலையைச் சூழ்ந்து கிடந்த வலையை யறப்பறித்து
புக்கினில் புக்குன்னைக் கண்டுகொண் டேனினிப் போக விடுவதுண்டே
மக்க ளறுவரைக் கல்லிடை மோத விழந்தவள் தன்வயிற்றில்
சிக்கென வந்து பிறந்துநின் றாய்திரு மாலிருஞ் சோலையெந்தாய்
en: Plucking at [the strings of this] net
that lays surrounded by vessels of suffering
in order to sever [it]
having entered the sweet abode [that you had] entered
and having seen you, I understand
How can [I] let [you] go now?
You who quickly came and were born in the womb of her
who lost six children when [they were] dashed between stones!
My Father of Tirumāliruñcōlai!
gloss: perfective aspect, feminine, singular, participial noun
participial noun, singular, vocative, second person, perfective aspect

ta: வளைத்துவைத் தேனினிப் போகலொட் டேனுன் தனிந்திர ஞாலங்களா
லொளித்திடில் நின்திரு வாணைகண் டாய்நீ யொருவர்க்கும் மெய்யனல்லை
யளித்தெங்கும் நாடும் நகரமுந் தம்முடைத் தீவினை தீர்க்கலுற்று
தெளித்து வலஞ்செய்யுந் தீர்த்த முடைத் திரு மாலிருஞ் சோலையெந்தாய்
en: Having caught [you] I kept you
[and] I cannot let you go now
Even if [you] conceal [yourself] with the magic arts!
You who observes [your] vow to Tiru are faithful to none other!
My Father of Tirumāliruñcōlai with the sacred waters
that circumambulate, creating clarity
causing the bad karma of cityfolk, countryfolk
and everyone everywhere else to vanish
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, second person, vocative
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

ta: உனக்குப் பணிசெய் திருக்குந் தவமுடை யேனினிப் போயொருவன்
தனக்குப் பணிந்து கடைத்தலை நிற்கைநின் சாயை யழிவுகண்டாய்
புனத்தினை கிள்ளிப் புதுவவி காட்டியுன் பொன்னடி வாழ்கவென்று
இனக்குற வர்புதிய துண்ணு மெழில்திரு மாலிருஞ் சோலையெந்தாய்
en: I have the tapas that occurs from doing service to you
[If] now [I] went [and] stood at the entrance
serving someone else
it would damage your fame, see!
My Father of beautiful Tirumāliruñcōlai where groups of hill people
pluck millet from the uplands, giving [them as] fresh offerings
saying “May your golden feet prosper!”
and [then] consuming the fresh cooked rice

ta: காதம் பலவுந் திரிந்துழன் றேற்கங்கோர் நிழலில்லை நீரில்லையுன்
பாத நிழலல்லால் மற்றோ ருயிர்ப்பிடம் நானெங்குங் காண்கின்றிலேன்
தூதுசென் றாய்குரு பாண்டவர்க் காயங்கோர் பொய்சுற்றம் பேசிசென்று
பேதஞ்செய் தெங்கும் பிணம்படைத் தாய்திரு மாலிருஞ் சோலையெந்தாய்
en: For me who wandered, whirling about for many miles
there is no shade, there is no water
except the shade of your feet
I do not see anywhere another place of refuge
You who came as a messenger, as the Pāṇḍavas’ guru
speaking of false kinship
You, my father of Tirumāliruñcōlai, sowing discord
created corpses everywhere
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, first person, singular, dative

ta: காலு மெழாகண்ண நீரும்நில் லாவுடல் சோர்ந்து நடுங்கிகுரல்
மேலு மெழாமயிர்க் கூச்சு மறாவென தோள்களும் வீழ்வொழியா
மாலு களாநிற்கு மென்மன னேயுன்னை வாழத்த லைப்பெய்திட்டேன்
சேலுக ளாநிற்கும் நீள்சுனை சூழ்திரு மாலிருஞ் சோலையெந்தாய்
en: [I] cannot lift [my] legs, [my] eyes won’t stop watering
[my] body languishes and quivers
[I] cannot raise [my] voice, [my] hair endlessly bristles
my shoulders unceasingly droop
my mind keeps slipping into delusion
I joined you in order to live!
My father in Tirumāliruñcōlai surrounded by wide pools
where carp leap

ta: எருத்துக் கொடியுடை யானும் பிரம னுமிந் திரனுமற்றும்
ஒருத்தரு மிப்பிற வியென்னும் நோய்க்கு மருந்தறி வாருமில்லை
மருத்துவ னாய்நின்ற மாமணி வண்ணா மறுபிற விதவிரத்
திருத்தியுங் கோயிற் கடைப்புகப் பெய்திரு மாலிருஞ் சோலையெந்தாய்
en: He with the bull banner, Brahmā, Indra and all the others
do not know the cure for the disease called ‘this birth’
Great Jewel Hued One who stands as the physician
mending in order to prevent any more births
make it so that [I] reach the entrance of your temple
my Father in Tirumāliruñcōlai
gloss: participial noun, third person, imperfective aspect

ta: அக்கரை யென்னு மனத்தக் கடலு ளழுந்தியுன் பேரருளால்
இக்கரை யேறியி ளைத்திருந் தேனையஞ் சேலென்று கைகவியாய்
சக்கர முந்தடக் கைகளுங் கண்களும் பீதக வாடையொடுஞ்
செக்கர் நிறத்துச் சிவப்புடை யாய்திரு மாலிருஞ் சோலையெந்தாய்
en: Saying, “Do not fear”, you extend your hand to me who
having sunk in the ocean of futility called the further shore
by the grace of your name
climbed, exhausted to this shore
My Father in Tirumāliruñcōlai
you who has the discus, broad hands and eyes
a golden garment, and a red hue the colour of the red sky
gloss: participial noun, singular, accusative, first person
participial noun, singular, vocative, second person

ta: எத்தனை காலமு மெத்தனை யூழியு மின்றொடு நாளையென்றே
இத்தனை காலமும் போய்க்கிறிப் பட்டே னினியுன்னைப் போகலொட்டேன்
மைத்துனன் மார்களை வாழ்வித்து மாற்றலர் நூற்றுவ ரைக்கெடுத்தாய்
சித்தம்நின் பால தறிதியன் றேதிரு மாலிருஞ் சோலையெந்தாய்
en: “How much time? How many eons? Today and tomorrow!”
all this time I was [caught] in lies
Now I cannot let you go!
You who caused [your] cousins to prosper
[and] destroyed [their] one-hundred enemies
Do you not know that [my] mind is on you
my Father in Tirumāliruñcōlai?
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect

ta: அன்று வயிற்றில் கிடந்திருந் தேயடி மைசெய்ய லுற்றிருப்பன்
இன்றுவந் திங்குன்னைக் கண்டுகொண் டேனினிப் போக விடுவதுண்டே
சென்றங்கு வாணனை யாயிரந் தோளுந் திருச்சக் கரமதனால்
தென்றித் திசைதிசை வீழச்செற் றாய்திரு மாலிருஞ் சோலையெந்தாய்
en: I, who have been loving and serving [you] since I lay in the womb
came here today and seeing you I took you in
How could I [let you] leave now?
My Father in Tirumāliruñcōlai
you who went there and killed Bāṇa with [your] blessed discus
scattering [his] thousand arms so that they fell
in every direction

ta: சென்றுல கங்குடைந் தாடுஞ் சுனைத்திரு மாலிருஞ் சோலைதன்னுள்
நின்ற பிரானடி மேலடி மைத்திறம் நேர்பட விண்ணப்பஞ்செய்
பொன்திகழ் மாடம் பொலிந்து தோன்றும் புதுவைக்கோன் விட்டுசித்தன்
ஒன்றினோ டொன்பதும் பாடவல் லாருல கமளந் தான்தமரே
en: Those who are able to sing [these] nine and one [verses]
by Viṭṭucittaṉ, king of Putuvai
where flourishing, golden, shining mansions are visible
that requests to be worthy of the service of the feet of the Lord
who stands in Tirumāliruñcōlai
with springs where the world comes to plunge deep and bathe
[they] are the kindred of He who measured the world
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: You of the cool high peaks of Tiruvēṅkaṭam!
Noble who remains so that the world may live!
Dāmodara! Fortune!
Having stampled myself and my possessions
with the mark of your discus
I have been longing for your grace
Now what is your holy design?
gloss: participial noun, singular, vocative, second person

en: Supreme God who rides the bird
after you took me by hand
great bliss has dried up the sea called birth
The forest of sin that causes death
has been seized by fire and burned
The river of nectar called knowledge
grasped my head and took my lips
gloss: neuter singular, third person, present tense

en: Our King! My family deity! My lord!
Who in this word will obtain the goodness
that was obtained by me who is inside you?
All the sin in the country that fell and was crushed
being just like one of us
was unable to breath and abandoned [me] fleeing
leaping into the bushes
As if filling a pot with nectar from the churned sea
[my] body melting, mouth opening
I took and drank of you [to my] fill
Swinging my stick, cruel Death won’t get to approach
O you with the broad mountian [like] shoulders
who weilds the discus!
Śārṅga bow warrior!
gloss: participial noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: Like taking gold and rubbing [it]
on a touchstone so that [its] colour will appear
I took you and placed [you] on my tongue
rubbing without change
I took and placed you inside me
I placed myself in you
My Father! My Hṛṣīkeśa! Guardian of my life!
I have taken and inscribed the impressions
of all your heroic deeds without omitting one
on the walls inside my heart
Noble Rāma who bears [his] axe
on [his] right side such that it subdues kings!
Our Lord, having come to me
now where is there to go?
Like the patriarch of the Pāṇṭiyas
who inscribed the Kayal fish on a mountain
you have inscribed [your] beautiful
auspicious red feet on my head
You have stripped me who has a tongue
that repeated copiously the words about you
“You who broke the tusk! You who killed the wrestler!”
[and] made [me] yours
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect, vocative
participial noun, vocative, second person, perfective aspect, singular
pronominalised noun, first person, singular, accusative

en: Having made Ananta and Garuḍa insignificant
you came to dwell inside my heart so that [I may] live
Contemplating [this] my lord
contemplating [the fact that you] remain in my heart
[and my heart] melting, so that tears overflow from [my] eyes
O Tall One with the discus, I have completed [my] toil
Having abandoned [your] practice of sleeping in the cool sea
[my] wonderous bridegroom, [my] Prince, able to come running
to live in the sea of my heart
while saying that the matchless sea
the matchless sun, the matchless world
are your homes, you stripped me [bare and] made me yours
Like a tall white banner that glitters and shines on a broad mountain
my splendorous Lord
who appears inside [my] heart as a brilliant light
forgetting [your] homes on the northern mountain
in Vaikunta, and in the walled city of Dvāraka
you have taken [your] home in me
Those who are able to sing about Gopala
who took [as his] temple the heart of Viṭṭucittaṉ
who was born into the clan of Vēyars
he with the complexion of a plump, cool cloud
the bull among herders, the king of the celestials
the nectar of brahmins
they will be as near [to Him] as a shadow
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
